# 52. Runtime Indicators

Track:

* memory headroom
* disk headroom
* event lag
* Twin freshness
* workflow backlog
* deploy failures.

---

# 53. Research Indicators

Track:

* unresolved final dataset choices
* incomplete baselines
* R2 promotions remaining open
* out-of-protocol rerun attempts.

---

# 54. Team Indicators

Track:

* components touched/reviewed by only one person
* owner overload
* undocumented handoffs.

---

# Objective Trigger Rules

## 55. TRG-01

If no complete E2E-01 dry-run path exists by mid-Sprint 5:

> CP-1 becomes AT_RISK.

---

# 56. TRG-02

If E2E-01 fails end Sprint 5:

> discretionary new capability work pauses.

---

# 57. TRG-03

If M3 fails:

> team-level recovery plan mandatory.

---

# 58. TRG-04

If M4 remains materially incomplete end Sprint 8:

> all S/R2 work suspended until F0/F1 recovery plan exists.

---

# 59. TRG-05

If M5 fails:

> M6 Research Freeze cannot proceed.

---

# 60. TRG-06

If M6 contains unresolved Dataset/Seed/Model/Policy/Metric choices:

> final benchmark cannot start.

---

# 61. TRG-07

If restore drill has not passed before final release:

> M8 cannot PASS.

---

# 62. TRG-08

If Oracle/final-test contamination is found:

> affected evidence invalidated.

---

# Risk Acceptance Authority

## 63. P3

Owner may accept with documentation.

---

# 64. P2

Owner + relevant reviewer.

---

# 65. P1

Owner + affected domain owner(s), visible in regular engineering review.

---

# 66. P0

Team-level review required.

---

# 67. Hard Invariant Violation Cannot Be Accepted by Vote

---

# Risk Review Cadence

## 68. Weekly

Review:

* new P0/P1
* triggered risks
* changed exposure
* upcoming milestone risks.

---

# 69. Sprint Planning

Review risks attached to critical-path items.

---

# 70. Milestone Exit

Re-score relevant open risks.

---

# 71. M6 / M7

Dedicated research-integrity risk review.

---

# 72. P2/P3 Need Not Consume Meeting Time Unless Changed

---

# Risk Aging

## 73. Risk Must Be Periodically Revalidated

---

# 74. No-Longer-Plausible Risk Is CLOSED

With reason.

---

# 75. Realized Risk Becomes TRIGGERED

And links to issue/incident.

---

# 76. Risk Without Owner Is Invalid

---

# 77. Risk Without Trigger / Indicator Is Usually Too Vague

---

# 78. Risk Without Threatened Capability Is Usually Not Actionable

---

# Residual Risk

## 79. Treatment Does Not Necessarily Eliminate Risk

RiskRecord should show:

> Initial Exposure → Treatment → Residual Exposure.

---

# 80. Score Reduction Requires Evidence

Mitigation code existing is not enough.

Its effectiveness must be validated.

---

# Risk vs Scope

## 81. Stretch Failure Normally Is Not Project-Critical

Unless optional capability was improperly introduced into mandatory critical path.

---

# 82. F1 Failure Is Different

Failure of mandatory:

* segmentation
* HITL
* Core
* Automation effect verification
* etc.

is real final-scope risk.

---

# Risk vs Technical Debt

## 83. Reduced Breadth May Become Debt

Only if mandatory semantics remain satisfied.

---

# 84. Missing Mandatory Invariant Is Not Debt

Example:

> no effect verification

cannot be accepted as technical debt.

---

# Risk vs ADR

## 85. Architecture-Changing Mitigation Requires ADR

---

# Risk vs Research

## 86. Research Risk Cannot Be “Fixed” Post Hoc

Unfavourable results do not justify methodology rewriting.

---

# 87. Frozen Stopping / Extension Rules Must Be Followed

Otherwise report inconclusive.

---

# Risk Anti-Patterns

## 88. Giant Ownerless Risk List

Rejected.

## 89. Every Risk Classified P0

Rejected.

## 90. Hiding Risk to Protect Milestone Status

Rejected.

## 91. Triggered Risk Left as Future Risk

Rejected.

## 92. Risk Register Used for Blame

Rejected.

## 93. Integrity Violation Accepted Due to Deadline

Rejected.

## 94. Risk Score Lowered Without Evidence

Rejected.

## 95. Risk Closed Before Mitigation Validation

Rejected.

---

# Risk Invariants

## RISK-INV-01

Risk, issue, blocker, debt and assumption remain distinct.

## RISK-INV-02

Every critical risk has one accountable owner.

## RISK-INV-03

Every critical risk identifies threatened capability/invariant and milestone.

## RISK-INV-04

Likelihood, impact and detectability guide prioritization but do not replace engineering judgment.

## RISK-INV-05

F0/security/research-integrity risks may override numerical score.

## RISK-INV-06

Low detectability increases monitoring importance.

## RISK-INV-07

Triggered risk becomes linked issue/incident/blocker.

## RISK-INV-08

Risk acceptance records rationale and residual exposure.

## RISK-INV-09

Hard integrity violations cannot be accepted away.

## RISK-INV-10

Late integration is treated as project-killer risk from project start.

## RISK-INV-11

Domain/Simulator validity is a first-class research risk.

## RISK-INV-12

Oracle leakage is always P0.

## RISK-INV-13

Train/final-test leakage affecting final evidence is P0.

## RISK-INV-14

Unsupported AI RCA is a critical product/research risk.

## RISK-INV-15

Infeasible Scheduler output is a hard failure independent of objective score.

## RISK-INV-16

Automation ACK without verified effect remains unacceptable.

## RISK-INV-17

Shared-host resource saturation is actively monitored.

## RISK-INV-18

Backup success cannot be claimed without restore validation.

## RISK-INV-19

Research Freeze cannot PASS with unresolved final choices.

## RISK-INV-20

Final benchmark validity has priority over feature overflow.

## RISK-INV-21

External assets cannot become uncontrolled core viability risks.

## RISK-INV-22

Bus-factor risk is monitored across every core subsystem.

## RISK-INV-23

Risk review is continuous and milestone-aware.

## RISK-INV-24

Stretch/R2 failure is not project failure unless capability was formally promoted.

## RISK-INV-25

Risk score decreases only after effectiveness evidence.

## RISK-INV-26

Architecture-changing mitigation follows ADR/review governance.

## RISK-INV-27

Research risks cannot be mitigated through post-hoc favourable methodology changes.

## RISK-INV-28

Risk management exists to surface uncertainty, not assign blame.

## RISK-INV-29

P0/P1 risks remain visible until closed or explicitly reduced to accepted residual risk.

## RISK-INV-30

Final release cannot PASS with unresolved triggered P0 risk affecting mandatory acceptance.

* prevention
* detection
* mitigation

---

# Nihai Karar

Platform Risk Management architecture:

> **Future uncertainty’yi Risk, realized failure’ı Issue, current progress stop condition’ını Blocker ve conscious compromise’ı Technical Debt olarak ayıran; Likelihood × Impact exposure ve independent Detectability dimension kullanan; P0 hard-invariant overrides ile product identity, security, authority, Oracle separation ve research validity’yi numerical scoring’in üzerinde koruyan; every critical risk’i owner, leading indicator, trigger, threatened capability/milestone ve residual risk ile bağlayan; CP-1 Product Closed Loop, CP-2 Research Evidence ve CP-3 Reproducibility critical paths üzerinden project-killer cascades’i takip eden continuous Risk Register**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

Ana prensipler:

**Risk ≠ Issue**

**Triggered Risk Becomes Concrete Work**

**Critical Integrity Overrides Arithmetic**

**Detect Hidden Risks Early**

**Late Integration Is a Project-Killer**

**Simulator Validity Is a Research Risk**

**Oracle Leakage Is Always P0**

**Ungrounded RCA Is a Critical AI Risk**

**Feasibility Before Scheduler Quality**

**ACK ≠ Verified Effect**

**Backup ≠ Recovery Until Restored**

**Research Freeze Must Be Real**

**Benchmark Integrity Beats Feature Overflow**

**Risk Scores Change Only With Evidence**

**Risk Management Is Not Blame**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

## Versiyon

**v1.0**

## Karar Tarihi

**13 Eylül 2026**



# 70 — Mitigation

## Durum

**Approved**

## Amaç

Intelligent Manufacturing Operations Platform for Critical Aerospace Components Risk Register’da tanımlanan risklerin yalnız listelenmesini değil;

* gerçekleşme olasılığının azaltılmasını,
* erken tespit edilmesini,
* trigger koşullarının tanımlanmasını,
* blast radius’unun sınırlandırılmasını,
* güvenli fallback davranışlarının belirlenmesini,
* recovery sürecinin işletilmesini,
* treatment effectiveness’in evidence ile doğrulanmasını,
* residual risk’in yeniden değerlendirilmesini

sağlayan canonical Risk Treatment architecture’ını tanımlamak.

Canonical treatment lifecycle:

> **Prevent → Detect → Trigger → Contain → Fallback → Recover → Verify → Re-score → Accept Residual Risk / Close**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

Ana prensipler:

> **A Mitigation Is Not Effective Because It Was Implemented; It Is Effective Only After Evidence Shows That It Changes Risk Exposure**

> **Fallback May Reduce Capability Quality or Availability; It May Not Violate Mandatory Correctness, Authority, Security, Oracle Isolation or Research-Integrity Invariants**

> **P0 Risks Require Defense in Depth**

---

# Risk Treatment Vocabulary

## 1. PREVENT

Risk’in gerçekleşme ihtimalini azaltan proactive control.

---

# 2. DETECT

Risk’in oluştuğunu veya yaklaşmakta olduğunu mümkün olduğunca erken ortaya çıkaran control.

---

# 3. TRIGGER

RiskRecord’ın:

> MONITORED → AT_RISK / TRIGGERED

durumuna geçmesini sağlayan objective condition.

---

# 4. CONTAIN

Triggered risk’in blast radius’unu durduran veya küçülten action.

---

# 5. FALLBACK

Primary implementation/capability güvenli veya kullanılabilir değilken devreye giren predesigned alternative.

---

# 6. RECOVER

Accepted normal/degraded operation’a dönüş süreci.

---

# 7. VERIFY

Mitigation, fallback veya recovery gerçekten doğru çalıştı mı sorusunun evidence-backed cevabı.

---

# 8. RESIDUAL RISK

Treatment sonrası kalan exposure.

---

# 9. Mitigation Is the Umbrella Concept

Mitigation tek action değil; yukarıdaki lifecycle’ın tamamıdır.

---

# Treatment Strategies

## 10. AVOID

Risk üreten design choice’u hiç yapmamak.

Example:

> external public data’yı core runtime dependency yapmamak.

---

# 11. REDUCE LIKELIHOOD

Risk’in oluşma ihtimalini düşürmek.

Example:

> protected main.

---

# 12. REDUCE IMPACT

Risk gerçekleşse bile sistem etkisini küçültmek.

Example:

> external provider abstraction.

---

# 13. INCREASE DETECTABILITY

Hidden risk’i erken observable hale getirmek.

---

# 14. ISOLATE

Blast radius’u architecture/access/data boundaries ile sınırlamak.

---

# 15. DEGRADE SAFELY

Capability quality/availability düşebilir; correctness korunur.

---

# 16. RECOVER

Canonical state’e veya accepted degraded mode’a dönmek.

---

# 17. ACCEPT

Treatment sonrası residual risk’in explicit olarak kabul edilmesi.

---

# 18. Risk Transfer Is Not a Primary Strategy

Third-party provider/service kullanımı technical risk’i ortadan kaldırmaz.

Often creates:

> external dependency risk.

---

# RiskTreatmentPlan

Every P0/P1 risk should have first-class:

> **RiskTreatmentPlan**

with minimum fields:

```text id="hpv5ju"
RiskTreatmentPlanID
RiskID
InitialRiskScore
TreatmentStrategy
PreventionControls
DetectionControls
LeadingIndicators
TriggerCondition
ContainmentActions
FallbackPlan
RecoveryActions
VerificationEvidence
TreatmentOwner
Responders
RequiredByMilestone
TreatmentStatus
ResidualLikelihood
ResidualImpact
ResidualDetectability
ResidualPriority
AcceptanceAuthority
EvidenceRefs
```

---

# Treatment Status

## 19. PLANNED

Treatment design exists.

---

# 20. IMPLEMENTED

Required control exists in code/config/process.

---

# 21. VERIFIED

Specific verification proves expected behavior.

---

# 22. EXERCISED

Risk/failure scenario has been deliberately induced or realistically exercised.

---

# 23. EFFECTIVE

Evidence supports actual exposure reduction.

---

# 24. IMPLEMENTED != EFFECTIVE

Example:

Backup job works:

> IMPLEMENTED.

Full restore succeeds:

> VERIFIED / EXERCISED.

Only then backup risk materially decreases.

---

# 25. P0 Closure Normally Requires VERIFIED

Recovery/resilience-related P0 preferably reaches:

> EXERCISED.

---

# Control Types

## 26. ARCHITECTURAL CONTROL

Example:

AI cannot access mutation API.

---

# 27. ACCESS CONTROL

Example:

Oracle credentials separated.

---

# 28. CONTRACT CONTROL

Example:

ApprovalDecision exact revision binding.

---

# 29. STATIC / CI CONTROL

Example:

architecture import tests.

---

# 30. RUNTIME CONTROL

Example:

container resource limits.

---

# 31. OBSERVABILITY CONTROL

Example:

Twin lag alert.

---

# 32. DATA CONTROL

Example:

group-aware SplitManifest.

---

# 33. RESEARCH CONTROL

Example:

ExperimentProtocolFreeze.

---

# 34. PROCESS CONTROL

Example:

CR-3 independent review.

---

# 35. RECOVERY CONTROL

Example:

full restore drill.

---

# 36. Defense in Depth Uses Different Control Types

Multiple manual checklists alone are not defense in depth.

---

# Treatment Priority

Default priority:

1. unresolved P0
2. imminent CP-1 / CP-2 / CP-3 P1
3. milestone-specific P1
4. P2
5. P3.

---

# 37. Mitigation Work Is First-Class Engineering Work

Examples:

* ScheduleValidator
* idempotency ledger
* Oracle ACL tests
* restore tooling
* drift detection.

These are not administrative overhead.

---

# Fallback Doctrine

## 38. Fallback Must Be Predesigned

Where technically possible.

---

# 39. Fallback Must Be Tested

Untested fallback is itself a risk.

---

# 40. Fallback State Must Be Observable

Relevant UI/telemetry should show:

* DEGRADED
* MANUAL_REQUIRED
* PAUSED
* UNAVAILABLE.

---

# 41. Fallback Cannot Fake Missing Capability

Example:

Vision unavailable → Oracle truth cannot be injected.

---

# 42. Fallback Cannot Bypass HITL

---

# 43. Fallback Cannot Bypass Core Validation

---

# 44. Fallback Cannot Bypass Research Freeze

---

# 45. Quality Reduction Is Allowed

Example:

CP-SAT timeout → validated heuristic.

Correctness retained; optimality may reduce.

---

# Capability Degradation States

Canonical states:

> **NORMAL
> DEGRADED
> MANUAL_REQUIRED
> PAUSED
> UNAVAILABLE**

---

# 46. Security / Authority Failure Mode Is Fail-Closed

Applies to:

* authentication
* authorization
* approvals
* protected commands
* Oracle boundaries.

---

# 47. Optional Capability Failure May Degrade

Examples:

* observability backend
* Valkey
* external AI provider.

---

# ARCH-R01 — Late Integration Treatment

## 48. Prevention

* M1 integrated spine
* E2E-01 by Sprint 5
* contract-first development
* short-lived branches
* fixture expiry milestones
* integration capacity reserved every sprint
* early draft PRs
* dependency board.

---

# 49. Detection

Indicators:

* critical mocks surviving beyond target milestone
* no successful E2E for > one sprint
* consumer not integrated to producer contract
* stale branch age
* CP-1 dependency AT_RISK.

---

# 50. Trigger

No complete E2E dry run by mid-Sprint 5.

---

# 51. Containment

Suspend:

* stretch
* R2 exploration
* noncritical polish
* unrelated technology work.

---

# 52. Fallback

Simplify internal algorithms only.

Allowed:

* deterministic triage
* heuristic Scheduler
* simple real Vision baseline.

---

# 53. Prohibited Fallback

Removing subsystem from loop.

---

# 54. Recovery

Focused integration swarm:

* producer
* consumer
* runtime owner
* one failing edge at a time.

---

# 55. Verification

E2E-01:

* happy path
* deterministic rerun
* authority negative path.

---

# ARCH-R02 — God-Service Treatment

## 56. Prevention

* ownership boundaries
* service/schema ownership
* private-import prohibition
* scoped service principals
* producer-owned contracts.

---

# 57. Detection

* architecture tests
* DB permission tests
* CODEOWNERS
* dependency scans.

---

# 58. Trigger

Any unauthorized:

* cross-schema mutation
* AI mutation endpoint
* private persistence import.

---

# 59. Containment

Block PR/deployment or revoke permission.

---

# 60. Recovery

Move behavior behind correct owner contract.

---

# 61. Verification

Architecture + negative access suite.

---

# ARCH-R04 — Semantic Contract Drift

## 62. Prevention

Contracts document:

* meaning
* units
* nullability
* confidence semantics
* versions
* examples.

---

# 63. Detection

Behavioral fixtures + consumer contract tests.

---

# 64. Trigger

Semantic meaning changes without explicit:

* BEHAVIORAL_CHANGE
* BREAKING.

---

# 65. Containment

Deployment/promotion blocked.

---

# 66. Recovery

Version contract or restore previous semantics.

---

# 67. Verification

Producer-consumer behavioral suite.

---

# 68. Schema Compatibility Alone Is Insufficient

Semantic compatibility must be validated.

---

# ARCH-R05 — Canonical Truth Ambiguity

## 69. Prevention

Canonical ownership:

* Core = business truth
* Simulator = simulated physical execution
* Twin = projection
* Scheduler = proposal
* Automation = execution state.

---

# 70. Detection

Reconciliation:

* Core revision
* Twin revision
* workflow expected effect.

---

# 71. Trigger

Multiple states claim canonical authority without defined reconciliation.

---

# 72. Containment

Mark state:

> STALE / VERIFY_REQUIRED.

---

# 73. Recovery

Replay/rebuild/reconcile correct projection.

---

# 74. Verification

Canonical-state invariant suite.

---

# ARCH-R08 — Replay Side Effects

## 75. Prevention

Projection replay and execution path are separate.

Replay principal has mutation-disabled credentials.

---

# 76. Detection

Replay side-effect test.

---

# 77. Trigger

Protected command generated during projection replay.

---

# 78. Containment

Stop replay immediately.

---

# 79. Recovery

Reconcile all affected states/effects.

---

# 80. Verification

Replay suite asserts:

> zero protected side effects.

---

# ARCH-R09 — Cross-World Contamination

## 81. Prevention

WorldID bound to:

* events
* queries
* object keys
* cache keys
* approvals
* manifests.

---

# 82. Detection

Negative world-isolation tests.

---

# 83. Trigger

World-A state visible/mutable through World-B context.

---

# 84. Containment

Affected experiments/world invalidated.

---

# 85. Recovery

Fresh clean WorldID + rerun.

---

# 86. Verification

World isolation suite.

---

# PLAN-R01 — Mandatory Scope Overload

## 87. Prevention

* F0/F1 baseline
* WIP limits
* R2/S isolation
* M4 feature-complete line
* no vanity feature accumulation.

---

# 88. Detection

Track:

* F1 milestone completion
* CP blockers
* stretch work started
* F1 still entering S9/S10.

---

# 89. Trigger

M4 materially incomplete at end S8.

---

# 90. Containment

Suspend:

* all S
* unpromoted R2
* optional integrations.

---

# 91. Fallback

Reduce breadth, never mandatory semantics.

---

# 92. Examples of Acceptable Breadth Reduction

* fewer model architectures
* fewer workflow variants
* fewer optional views
* one CP-SAT formulation.

---

# 93. Recovery

Replan only remaining F0/F1 against critical path.

---

# 94. Verification

M4 mandatory capability matrix.

---

# 95. F1 Demotion Is Scope Change, Not Mitigation

---

# PLAN-R07 / RES-R09 — Research Freeze Slip

## 96. Prevention

Staged freeze:

* data/scenario candidate freeze
* baseline/model/policy selection
* final protocol freeze.

---

# 97. Detection

Freeze readiness shows:

* open datasets
* unfrozen seeds
* unselected models
* open R2 promotions
* TBD metrics.

---

# 98. Trigger

Any final behavioral decision remains TBD at M6.

---

# 99. Containment

Final benchmark blocked.

---

# 100. Fallback

Use already-accepted mandatory baseline.

Example:

ColBERT undecided → do not promote.

---

# 101. Recovery

Finish calibration, create new freeze version.

---

# 102. Verification

CR-4 independent freeze review.

---

# 103. Late R2 Candidate Defaults to Non-Promotion

Never benchmark delay by default.

---

# TEAM-R01 — Bus Factor

## 104. Prevention

* secondary familiarity
* cross review
* runbooks
* contracts
* no personal-only scripts
* reproducible local environment.

---

# 105. Detection

Risk indicators:

* no non-owner review for >2 sprints
* secondary cannot build/run subsystem
* undocumented setup.

---

# 106. Trigger

Owner unavailable and no qualified secondary can operate core path.

---

# 107. Containment

Freeze risky changes.

---

# 108. Fallback

Run last-known-good artifact.

---

# 109. Recovery

Formal ownership handoff.

---

# 110. Verification

Secondary teammate independently:

* builds
* tests
* diagnoses basic failure.

---

# TEAM-R03 — Asrın Bottleneck

## 111. Prevention

Review distribution:

* AI/Vision → Selman
* AI/Automation → Batu
* runtime/security → Yavuz.

---

# 112. Detection

Reviewer queue age.

---

# 113. Trigger

Multiple CP PRs blocked on a single reviewer.

---

# 114. Containment

Qualified reviewer reassignment.

---

# 115. Recovery

Increase cross-domain familiarity and normative docs.

---

# TEAM-R06 — Batu Overload

## 116. Prevention

Sequenced depth:

1. DES
2. baseline Scheduler
3. Automation skeleton
4. CP-SAT depth
5. advanced recovery.

---

# 117. Detection

* promoted local LLM

* use legitimate configured fallback,
* do not pretend fallback result came from primary LLM.

# Mitigation Invariants

## MIT-INV-01

Every P0/P1 risk must have an explicit RiskTreatmentPlan.

## MIT-INV-02

Treatment distinguishes prevention, detection, containment, fallback, recovery and verification.

## MIT-INV-03

Implemented control does not lower risk exposure without effectiveness evidence.

## MIT-INV-04

P0 treatment normally requires integration-level or stronger verification.

## MIT-INV-05

High-D risks require deliberate negative testing.

## MIT-INV-06

Critical runtime dependencies use predefined safe fallback where possible.

## MIT-INV-07

Fallback may reduce quality but cannot violate correctness, authority, security or research integrity.

## MIT-INV-08

Authentication/authorization failure for protected operation fails closed.

## MIT-INV-09

AI/provider failure cannot produce mutation-authority fallback.

## MIT-INV-10

Scheduler timeout falls back only to validated feasible planning strategy.

## MIT-INV-11

Automation timeout cannot blindly retry protected non-idempotent effect.

## MIT-INV-12

Protected workflow completion requires verified effect.

## MIT-INV-13

Oracle leakage invalidates contaminated downstream evidence.

## MIT-INV-14

Train/test leakage invalidates affected model/evaluation evidence.

## MIT-INV-15

Late integration is mitigated through simpler real internals rather than fake subsystem bypass.

## MIT-INV-16

Scope overload removes stretch/R2 breadth before mandatory semantics.

## MIT-INV-17

Late R2 candidate defaults to non-promotion.

## MIT-INV-18

Research Freeze cannot contain unresolved TBD behavioral choices.

## MIT-INV-19

Backup risk materially decreases only after restore verification.

## MIT-INV-20

Shared-host resource policy protects correctness-critical services before convenience/background workloads.

## MIT-INV-21

Observability backend failure cannot normally take down canonical business services.

## MIT-INV-22

Drifted environment is ineligible for formal evidence.

## MIT-INV-23

Secret exposure requires revoke/rotate, not only repository cleanup.

## MIT-INV-24

External-data/license risk falls back to approved or owned synthetic data.

## MIT-INV-25

Synthetic/public domain mismatch produces bounded claims instead of misleading aggregation.

## MIT-INV-26

Negative/inconclusive results cannot trigger favorable post-hoc methodology changes.

## MIT-INV-27

Benchmark-size reduction preserves predeclared primary design.

## MIT-INV-28

Demo fallback is transparent and cannot impersonate unavailable primary capability.

## MIT-INV-29

Recovery is incomplete until downstream contamination/state correctness is checked.

## MIT-INV-30

Residual risk is explicitly re-scored after treatment evidence.

18. Bus-factor mitigation secondary operational familiarity sağlamalıdır.

21. Synthetic shortcut learning challenge sets ile tested olmalıdır.

55. Mitigation effectiveness actual risk behavior üzerinden ölçülmelidir.

# Açık Sorular

Madde 70 kapsamında mitigation architecture’a ilişkin kritik açık soru bulunmamaktadır.

Implementation phase’da refine edilebilecek details:

* exact alert thresholds
* exact resource limits
* exact fallback latency budgets
* exact OOD thresholds
* exact review timers
* exact storage warning percentages
* exact treatment evidence serialization.

Bunlar accepted treatment semantics’i değiştirmeyecektir.

---

# Nihai Karar

Platform Mitigation architecture:

> **P0/P1 risks’i Prevention, Detection, Trigger, Containment, Fallback, Recovery, Verification ve Residual-Risk stages üzerinden yöneten; implemented control ile proven-effective control’ü ayıran; critical risks için defense-in-depth ve deliberate negative testing uygulayan; fallback’lerin quality azaltmasına izin verirken correctness, authority, security, Oracle isolation ve research integrity’yi ihlal etmesini yasaklayan; treatment effectiveness’i actual behavior evidence ile ölçen ve mitigation’ın protected milestone’dan önce verified olmasını zorunlu kılan risk-treatment system**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

Ana treatment packages:

> **Integration Survival Package**

> **Research Integrity Package**

> **AI Grounding Package**

> **Scheduling Safety Package**

> **Automation Safety Package**

> **Single-Host Reliability Package**

> **Scope Survival Package**

> **Final Evidence Survival Package**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

Ana prensipler:

**Prevent Before Recover**

**Detect Before Damage Spreads**

**Contain Before Repair**

**Fallback Must Be Safe**

**Implemented ≠ Effective**

**P0 Requires Defense in Depth**

**Timeout ≠ Blind Retry**

**ACK ≠ Verified Effect**

**Failure May Reduce Quality, Never Authority**

**Oracle Contamination Propagates**

**Leakage Invalidates Evidence**

**Late Research Candidate → Do Not Promote**

**Backup Must Be Restored**

**Drifted Environment Cannot Produce Formal Evidence**

**Demo Contingency Must Be Transparent**

**Research Mitigation Cannot Change the Story After Seeing Results**

**Residual Risk Must Be Re-Scored With Evidence**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

# 71 — Technical Debt

## Durum

**Approved**

## Amaç

Intelligent Manufacturing Operations Platform for Critical Aerospace Components geliştirme sürecinde bilinçli olarak kabul edilen engineering compromise’ları:

* eksik mandatory scope’tan,
* mevcut bug/issue’dan,
* blocker’dan,
* future risk’ten,
* security/authority/research-integrity violation’dan

kesin biçimde ayırmak ve gerçek technical debt’i:

* principal,
* interest,
* owner,
* acceptance authority,
* repayment trigger,
* LatestCarryMilestone,
* verification
* residual debt

üzerinden yönetmek.

Canonical debt lifecycle:

> **Identify Compromise → Verify Invariants Still Hold → Record Principal → Estimate Interest → Assign Owner → Set Repayment Trigger → Set Latest Carry Milestone → Monitor Interest → Repay / Convert / Escalate**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

Ana prensipler:

> **Technical Debt Is a Conscious Implementation Compromise, Not Missing Mandatory Work**

> **Debt Is Allowed Only When Current Capability Semantics and Acceptance Invariants Still Hold**

> **Missing Mandatory Capability Is Scope Failure, Not Debt**

> **Security, Authority, Oracle Isolation and Research Integrity Cannot Be Financed With Technical Debt**

---

# Concept Separation

## 1. Risk

Henüz gerçekleşmemiş future uncertainty.

---

# 2. Issue / Bug

Şu anda mevcut yanlış behavior veya defect.

---

# 3. Blocker

Aktif work’ü şu anda durduran condition.

---

# 4. Scope Gap

Accepted mandatory capability’nin hiç bulunmaması veya acceptance semantics’inin karşılanmaması.

---

# 5. Acceptance Failure

Hard final/milestone invariant’ın karşılanmaması.

---

# 6. Technical Debt

Capability doğru ve accepted semantics içinde çalışırken, gelecekte ek engineering cost yaratacağı bilinerek kabul edilen implementation compromise.

---

# 7. ScopeDebt

Mandatory semantics korunurken yalnız breadth/generality’nin bilinçli azaltılması.

ScopeDebt yalnız bu şart altında Technical Debt ile ilişkilendirilebilir.

---

# Canonical Classification Examples

| Situation                                                                    | Classification                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Future Temporal restart problem may occur                                    | Risk                                                                               |
| Temporal restart currently loses approval                                    | Issue                                                                              |
| E2E cannot proceed until fixed                                               | Blocker                                                                            |
| Segmentation does not exist                                                  | Scope Gap                                                                          |
| Approval replay succeeds                                                     | Acceptance/Security Failure                                                        |
| Selected workflows support bounded compensation instead of generic framework | Technical/Scope Debt                                                               |
| CP-SAT has one formulation instead of multiple research formulations         | Technical/Scope Debt                                                               |
| Final training requires undocumented notebook cells                          | High-interest ML debt before deadline; final acceptance failure if carried too far |

---

# Debt Qualification Gate

A compromise can enter the Technical Debt Register only if all following conditions hold.

## 8. Current Capability Semantics Pass

Required.

---

# 9. No Hard Invariant Is Violated

Required.

---

# 10. Current Milestone Exit Remains Valid

Required.

---

# 11. Future Engineering Cost Exists

Required.

Otherwise the decision may simply be legitimate architecture.

---

# 12. Repayment Can Be Meaningfully Defined

Required.

---

# 13. Failed Qualification Means Debt Classification Is Rejected

The item must instead become appropriate:

* Issue
* Risk
* Scope Gap
* Acceptance Failure
* ADR.

# Debt Principal

Principal represents:

> effort/structural complexity required to repay debt today.

Canonical classes:

## 29. P-S

# 32. P-XL

# Debt Interest

Debt interest represents ongoing cost created while debt remains.

Interest dimensions may include:

* development friction
* review friction
* defect probability
* integration friction
* operational burden
* performance cost
* resource cost
* reproducibility cost
* research-iteration cost
* onboarding/bus-factor cost.

Canonical levels:

## 34. I0 — Negligible

---

# 35. I1 — Low

---

# 36. I2 — Moderate

---

# 37. I3 — High

---

# 38. I4 — Critical / Compounding

---

# 39. Principal and Interest Are Independent

A small fix can have high recurring interest.

A large refactor may have low current interest.

---

# 40. Debt Priority Favors High Interest

High-interest debt on active critical paths takes precedence over large but dormant cleanup.

---

# Interest Evidence

Useful indicators include:

* repeated bugs
* repeated workaround code
* duplicate mappings/logic
* repeated deployment incidents
* setup friction
* benchmark overhead
* repeated manual steps
* flaky tests
* model retraining friction
* migration friction
* recurring review comments.

---

# Debt Lifecycle

Canonical states:

> **PROPOSED
> → ACCEPTED
> → ACTIVE
> → DUE
> → REPAYING
> → CLOSED**

Exceptional states:

> **BREACHED**

and:

> **CONVERTED**

---

# 41. PROPOSED

Compromise is being considered.

Not yet approved.

---

# 42. ACCEPTED

Relevant authority approves intentional compromise.

---

# 43. ACTIVE

Debt exists in accepted implementation.

---

# 44. DUE

Repayment trigger or LatestCarryMilestone reached.

---

# 45. REPAYING

Debt-removal work is active.

---

# 46. CLOSED

Debt removed and verification passed.

---

# 47. BREACHED

Debt passed permitted carry point.

BREACHED debt triggers:

* Issue
* Risk reassessment
* milestone impact review.

---

# 48. CONVERTED

Debt is formally reclassified.

Possible destinations:

* ADR-backed permanent design
* Issue
* Scope Gap.

---

# 49. Debt Cannot Close Because Team Chose to Ignore It

Closure requires:

* repayment, or
* formal architectural conversion.

---

# Debt Acceptance Authority

## 50. D0 — Local Debt

Localized, low-interest, noncritical.

Acceptance:

> owner + reviewer.

---

# 51. D1 — Component Debt

Subsystem maintainability/integration impact.

Acceptance:

> component owner + reviewer.

---

# 52. D2 — Cross-Domain Debt

Contract/runtime/dependency effect.

Acceptance:

> affected domain owners + cross-review.

---

# 53. D3 — Architectural / Critical-Path Debt

Includes:

* P-L/P-XL
* I3/I4
* CP-1/CP-2/CP-3 impact
* milestone impact.

Acceptance:

> team-level review.

ADR considered/required depending architecture effect.

---

# 54. Significant Debt Cannot Be Self-Accepted

---

# LatestCarryMilestone

Every material debt must specify an explicit latest allowed carry point.

Possible examples:

* M1
* M2
* E2E-01
* M3
* M4
* M5
* M6
* M8
* POST-PROJECT.

---

# 55. Debt Without LatestCarryMilestone Is Invalid

“Later” is not a repayment policy.

---

# 56. POST-PROJECT Is Restricted

Only debt that cannot invalidate:

* final acceptance
* reproducibility
* security
* research evidence
* demo correctness

may carry POST-PROJECT.

---

# Milestone Debt Gates

# Before E2E-01

Potentially carryable:

* internal code duplication
* basic UI polish debt
* limited baseline generality.

Not carryable:

* fake service boundaries
* direct DB mutation
* fake authentication
* missing required effect verification.

---

# Before M4

All F0/F1 capabilities must exist.

Allowed debt:

> reduced generality or implementation elegance.

Forbidden:

> mandatory capability absent.

---

# Before M5

High-interest:

* reliability
* testing
* performance
* operational-diagnostics

debt must be substantially cleared.

M5 means:

> Reliability & Evaluation Ready.

---

# Before M6

Research-critical debt must be nearly eliminated.

Cannot carry unresolved debt affecting:

* Experiment artifact identity
* Dataset reproducibility
* Model/config provenance
* Analysis correctness
* Benchmark environment binding
* Manual setup capable of changing results.

---

# 57. M6 Is Research-Critical Debt Freeze

---

# Before M8

No unresolved debt may invalidate:

* F0/F1/R1 acceptance
* DR
* authority
* security
* repeatability
* final demo
* thesis evidence.

---

# Final Release Debt Policy

## 58. Zero Debt Is Not Required

Zero-debt final release is unrealistic and unnecessary.

---

# 59. Residual Debt Must Be Bounded

Final-carriable debt must be:

* known
* documented
* semantics-preserving
* noncritical
* non-security-sensitive
* non-research-contaminating.

---

# Examples of Final-Carriable Debt

* internal helper duplication
* low-impact UI refactor
* noncritical DX inconvenience
* optional extension point deferred
* noncritical dashboard ergonomics.

---

# Examples Not Carriable to Final

* flaky final benchmark
* unproven restore
* missing mandatory Vision capability
* unsafe workflow retry
* manual untracked deployment
* approval replay
* unknown dataset redistribution rights
* evidence/provenance ambiguity.

---

# Forbidden Technical Debt

The following are never valid debt classifications.

## 60. Missing F0 Capability

Forbidden.

---

# 61. Missing F1 Capability

Forbidden.

---

# 62. Unauthorized Mutation Path

Forbidden.

---

# 63. AI Mutation Credential

Forbidden.

---

# 64. Missing Exact Approval Binding

Forbidden.

---

# 65. Missing Effect Verification

Forbidden.

---

# 66. Oracle Leakage

Forbidden.

---

# 67. Train/Test Leakage

Forbidden.

---

# 68. Final-Test Contamination

Forbidden.

---

# 69. Known Invalid Baseline Comparison

Forbidden.

---

# 70. Restricted Dataset Publication

Forbidden.

---

# 71. Exposed Secret

Forbidden.

---

# 72. Unverified Final Restore

Cannot be labeled debt at M8.

---

# 73. Known Infeasible Scheduler Output

Bug/hard failure.

---

# 74. False Twin Freshness

Correctness failure.

---

# Architecture Debt

## 75. Architecture Debt Has High Compound Interest

It affects future work across multiple components.

---

# 76. Architecture Debt Expires Earlier Than Equivalent Local Code Debt

Default policy.

---

# 77. P-XL Architecture Debt Requires ADR-Level Review

---

# Acceptable Temporary Architecture Debt Example

Duplicated bounded adapter implementation awaiting safe extraction.

---

# Invalid Architecture “Debt”

Scheduler writes directly to Core persistence because API is unfinished.

This is:

> boundary violation.

Not debt.

---

# Contract Debt

Examples that may be valid:

* temporary adapter
* bounded v1/v2 compatibility period
* nonideal field naming preserved for compatibility.

---

# 78. Contract Debt Cannot Create Semantic Ambiguity

Silent meaning changes remain defects/risks.

---

# Testing Debt

Temporary test debt may exist during active development.

Example:

> component deterministic tests exist, but desired broad property suite is incomplete.

Potentially valid before relevant gate.

---

# 79. Critical Security/Authority Test Gaps Expire Early

Examples:

* stale approval
* authorization
* idempotency
* Oracle access
* ScheduleValidator.

---

# 80. Critical-Path Test Debt Cannot Survive Relevant Milestone

---

# Data Debt

Potentially valid:

> analytics pipeline currently full-rebuild instead of incremental.

---

# 81. Dataset Identity Cannot Be Debt

Missing exact dataset identity/checksum required by final pipeline is acceptance/provenance failure.

---

# 82. Split Integrity Cannot Be Debt

---

# 83. Required Provenance Cannot Be Debt

---

# ML / Vision Debt

Potentially valid:

* deployment batch size manually tuned
* model-serving optimization deferred
* internal training-pipeline cleanup.

---

# Invalid ML/Vision Debt

Missing:

* localization
* segmentation
* anomaly
* OOD

is scope gap.

---

# 84. Final Training Cannot Depend on Undocumented Notebook State

---

# 85. Notebook-Dependent Reproducibility Debt Expires Before M5/M6

---

# AI / RAG Debt

Potentially valid:

> duplicated retriever deployment metadata while canonical authority remains explicit.

---

# Invalid AI/RAG Debt

* unsupported RCA evidence
* missing claim/citation binding where required
* RAG becoming operational truth.

---

# 86. RAG Debt Cannot Violate Documentary-vs-Operational Boundary

---

# Scheduler Debt

Potentially valid:

* only one CP-SAT formulation
* limited warm-start work
* no advanced stochastic solver
* manually configured objective weights.

---

# Invalid Scheduler Debt

* missing independent validator
* unbounded solve behavior
* infeasible plans reaching execution.

---

# 87. Optimization Sophistication May Carry Debt

---

# 88. Feasibility Cannot Carry Debt

---

# Automation Debt

Potentially valid:

> compensation implemented only for selected core workflow families rather than generic saga framework.

---

# Invalid Workflow Debt

* unsafe retry
* transient approval state
* ACK treated as verified success
* no freshness check
* non-idempotent protected effects.

---

# 89. Workflow Generality May Be Debt

---

# 90. Workflow Safety Cannot Be Debt

---

# Platform Debt

Potentially valid:

* Compose duplication
* imperfect `mfgctl` ergonomics
* versioned-but-manual certificate procedure
* low-impact infrastructure cleanup.

---

# Invalid Platform Debt

* SSH required for normal application deployment
* mutable final artifacts
* Integration snowflake
* secrets in Git
* unreconstructable runtime.

---

# Observability Debt

Potentially valid:

* limited noncritical dashboards
* some background workers only generic metrics.

---

# 91. Critical Diagnosability Cannot Be Debt by M5

Required:

* correlation
* capability health
* host/resource visibility
* critical workflow visibility.

---

# Performance Debt

## 92. Performance Debt Is Valid Only Inside Accepted Hard Boundary

Example:

Ideal:

> 80 ms.

Observed:

> 150 ms.

NFR hard limit:

> 250 ms.

Potential debt.

If hard NFR is violated:

> Issue / acceptance failure.

---

# Documentation Debt

Potentially valid:

* advanced tutorial incomplete
* optional explanatory diagrams missing.

---

# Invalid Final Documentation Debt

If missing documentation prevents:

* deployment
* restore
* benchmark reproduction
* operational diagnosis,

it cannot remain debt at final release.

---

# 93. Normative Documentation Has Earlier Deadline Than Optional Educational Documentation

---

# Developer Experience Debt

Legitimate examples:

* setup requires two canonical commands instead of one
* error output is poor
* local profile UX is awkward.

---

# 94. Daily Repeated DX Friction May Be High-Interest

Even when principal is small.

---

# Research-Infrastructure Debt

Early valid examples:

* manual orchestration among versioned scripts
* incomplete experiment-launch ergonomics.

---

# Invalid Research-Infrastructure Debt Before M6

Anything capable of causing:

* wrong artifact binding
* irreproducible results
* metric ambiguity
* evidence loss.

---

# 95. Research Tooling Convenience May Carry Debt

---

# 96. Research Validity Cannot Carry Debt

---

# Debt Introduction

## 97. Intentional Debt Should Be Declared Before Merge

Preferably in originating PR.

---

# 98. Retrospective Debt Discovery Is Allowed

Some debt becomes apparent only after repeated use.

---

# 99. Known Material Debt Must Not Remain Undocumented

---

# PR Integration

Meaningful PR template should include:

> **Introduces Technical Debt? YES / NO**

If YES:

* DebtID
* justification
* LatestCarryMilestone.

---

# TODO Policy

## 100. TODO Is Not the Debt Register

---

# 101. Small Local Cleanup TODO Is Allowed

Only when truly localized/nonmaterial.

---

# 102. Architectural / Cross-Service / Milestone-Relevant TODO Requires DebtID

---

# 103. Anonymous Architectural TODO Is Prohibited

---

# Debt Budget

Debt budget is not item-count based.

---

# 104. Count-Only Debt Budget Is Rejected

One P-XL/I4 debt may be more damaging than many P-S/I1 debts.

---

# 105. Critical-Path Debt Limit

No critical-path capability should carry more than one ACTIVE I3/I4 debt without explicit team review.

---

# 106. Owner-Level Debt Concentration Is Monitored

Avoid multiple high-interest debts expiring simultaneously under one owner.

---

# 107. M4 Architectural Debt Appetite Falls Sharply

New D3/architectural debt after feature complete is exceptional.

---

# 108. M5+ New-Debt Appetite Is Low

---

# 109. M6+ Research-Critical Debt Appetite Is Near Zero

---

# Debt Saturation

A component is debt-saturated when:

* new work repeatedly works around old debt
* multiple high-interest debts overlap same dependency path
* ordinary changes first require debt workarounds
* recurring defects originate from debt region.

---

# 110. Debt Saturation Is a Trigger

New feature development in affected area may pause until repayment.

---

# Debt Review Cadence

No separate debt meeting required.

## 111. Weekly

Review only:

* new high-interest
* newly DUE
* BREACHED debt.

---

# 112. Sprint Planning

Review debt attached to planned critical-path components.

---

# 113. M4

Mandatory feature-complete debt audit.

---

# 114. M5

Reliability/evaluation debt audit.

---

# 115. M6

Research/evidence debt audit.

---

# 116. M8

Final residual-debt audit.

---

# Repayment Triggers

Every material debt has one or more concrete triggers.

Possible examples:

* second defect attributable to debt
* repeated workaround threshold reached
* next contract version
* next training cycle
* affected component becomes critical path
* performance threshold approached
* milestone M5/M6 begins
* owner handoff starts.

---

# 117. “When We Have Time” Is Invalid

---

# Repayment Priority

Use qualitative relation:

> **Interest × Criticality × Imminence**

Questions:

* Is interest compounding?
* Does it affect F0/F1?
* Is it on CP-1/CP-2/CP-3?
* Is expiry near?
* Does it cause repeated defects?
* Does it block teammates?
* Will repayment become more expensive later?

---

# 118. High Interest + Critical Path + Near Expiry = Immediate Priority

---

# Debt Repayment Workflow

Debt repayment follows normal Team Workflow.

Required:

* linked DebtID
* short-lived branch
* CI
* review
* regression evidence
* closure verification.

---

# 119. Debt Repayment Is Not Hidden Cleanup

---

# 120. Debt Closes Only After Verification

---

# Prevention of Unnecessary Debt

Existing mechanisms:

* contract-first design
* ownership boundaries
* ADRs
* short-lived PRs
* automated CI
* generated OpenAPI clients
* common testkit
* immutable manifests
* `mfgctl`.

---

# Speculative Complexity Debt

## 121. Over-Abstraction Can Also Be Debt

Premature generic framework building can create high-interest complexity.

Examples rejected as unnecessary generalization:

* generic BPMN engine
* generic DES framework
* custom orchestration platform
* schema-registry platform
* microservice-per-entity abstraction.

---

# 122. YAGNI Applies to Speculative Generalization

---

# 123. YAGNI Does Not Justify Removing Accepted F1 Capability

---

# Reasonable Platform Debt Examples

## 124. TD-WF Example

Only core recovery workflows have explicit compensation.

No generic compensation DSL.

Potentially carryable POST-PROJECT if all mandatory workflow acceptance passes.

---

# 125. TD-SCHED Example

Only one well-validated CP-SAT formulation.

Potentially converts into final design rather than debt.

---

# 126. TD-DX Example

`mfgctl` error formatting is incomplete.

Possible final residual debt.

---

# 127. TD-OBS Example

Noncritical background worker lacks specialized dashboard.

Possible final residual debt.

---

# 128. TD-CODE Example

Two bounded adapters duplicate mapping logic.

Temporary technical debt.

---

# Invalid Debt Examples

## 129. “Segmentation Not Finished”

Scope Gap.

---

# 130. “AI Hallucinates Unsupported Cause”

AI quality/risk issue.

---

# 131. “Approval Replay Works”

P0 authority/security issue.

---

# 132. “No Off-Host Backup at M8”

Acceptance failure.

---

# 133. “Final Test Was Used for Tuning”

Research-integrity violation.

---

# 134. “Scheduler Emits Infeasible Plans”

Bug/hard failure.

---

# ScopeDebt Relationship

## 135. ScopeDebt Is Valid Only When Accepted Semantics Remain Complete

---

# Example

Desired architecture:

> generalized compensation framework.

Actual accepted implementation:

> explicit compensation for selected mandatory workflows.

If accepted F1 semantics pass:

> valid ScopeDebt.

If mandatory workflow lacks required compensation:

> Scope Gap.

---

# Debt and Risk Coupling

## 136. I3/I4 Debt Requires Risk Impact Check

If debt increases future uncertainty:

> link RiskRecord.

---

# 137. Debt Does Not Replace Risk

Debt represents known compromise.

Risk represents uncertain consequence.

---

# Debt and ADR

## 138. Temporary Deviation From Accepted ADR

DebtRecord required.

---

# 139. New Intentional Architecture

ADR required.

---

# 140. Chronic Debt May Become Architecture Reassessment

Repeated failed repayment may indicate:

> chosen “debt” is actually appropriate architecture.

Then convert through ADR, not silent permanence.

---

# Debt and Tests

## 141. Defect-Prone Debt Repayment Should Add Regression Test

Where practical.

---

# 142. Architecture-Debt Repayment Should Add Architecture Test

Where practical.

---

# 143. Repayment Should Reduce Reintroduction Probability

---

# Debt Ownership

## 144. Debt Has Exactly One Current Owner

Normally aligned with affected capability owner.

---

# 145. Ownership Transfer Explicitly Transfers Debt

---

# 146. Debt Cannot Become Orphaned

---

# Debt Branch Policy

## 147. No Long-Lived “tech-debt-cleanup” Branch

Debt repayment uses normal short-lived branch/PR flow.

---

# Debt and Thesis

Final residual debt can appear under:

* limitations
* future work
* engineering tradeoffs

where academically relevant.

---

# 148. Debt Cannot Excuse Missing Requirement in Thesis

---

# Portfolio Interpretation

A well-governed debt decision may demonstrate:

* engineering judgment
* prioritization
* architecture tradeoffs
* complexity control.

Example:

> bounded workflow compensation intentionally chosen instead of generic saga framework.

Narrative must include:

* rationale
* consequences
* guardrails.

---

# 149. “We Ran Out of Time” Is Not Sufficient Debt Rationale

---

# Debt Metrics

Avoid vanity:

> total debt count.

Prefer:

* I3/I4 debt count
* BREACHED debt
* CP-1/2/3 debt
* debt due before next milestone
* debt causing repeated defects
* debt with multiple deadline extensions.

---

# 150. Debt Count Is Not a Quality Metric

---

# FinalResidualDebtRegister

At M8 create:

> **FinalResidualDebtRegister**

for intentionally open debt.

Each record includes:

* DebtID
* why still open
* why final acceptance remains valid
* residual risk
* limitation created
* future repayment recommendation.

---

# 151. M8 Cannot PASS With BREACHED Debt Affecting F0/F1/R1

---

# Debt Expiry

When LatestCarryMilestone passes:

1. status → BREACHED
2. linked Issue created
3. Risk reassessed
4. dependent new work may be blocked
5. team chooses:

   * repay immediately,
   * convert to ADR,
   * formally rebaseline scope.

---

# 152. Silent Expiry Extension Is Forbidden

---

# 153. Deadline Extension Uses Same-or-Higher Acceptance Authority

---

# 154. Second Extension Triggers Architecture/Scope Review

Repeated extensions are a red flag.

---

# Debt Appetite by Phase

| Phase    | Debt Appetite                              |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| S1–S2    | Moderate                                   |
| S3–S4    | Moderate; boundary debt low                |
| S5–S6    | Low on CP-1                                |
| S7–S8    | Moderate local / low architectural         |
| S9–S10   | Low                                        |
| S11 / M6 | Very Low                                   |
| S12 / M7 | Near Zero for behavior/evidence            |
| S13 / M8 | Only bounded residual maintainability debt |

---

# 155. Debt Appetite Falls Toward Research Freeze

---

# Post-M6 Debt Rule

After M6, new debt affecting:

* model behavior
* retrieval behavior
* scheduling behavior
* workflow behavior
* dataset identity
* metric identity
* experiment environment

is prohibited by default.

Critical fixes may still happen, but affected:

* freeze
* experiments
* evidence

must be reconsidered.

---

# 156. M6 Is a Technical-Debt Freeze for Research-Critical Paths

---

# Emergency Debt

A hotfix may occasionally create temporary:

> **EmergencyDebt**

under strict conditions.

---

# 157. Emergency Debt Must Restore, Not Weaken, Safety/Correctness

---

# 158. Emergency Debt Is Recorded in Same Incident/Hotfix Flow

---

# 159. Emergency Debt Has Near-Term LatestCarryMilestone

---

# 160. Emergency Debt Automatically Becomes DUE After Stabilization

---

# 161. Retrospective Review Is Mandatory

---

# 162. Emergency Debt Cannot Become Permanent Through Neglect

---

# Debt Closure Verification Classes

## 163. DV-1 — Code Review

Localized debt.

---

# 164. DV-2 — Component Regression

Subsystem behavior.

---

# 165. DV-3 — Integration Regression

Cross-boundary debt.

---

# 166. DV-4 — Performance / Resource Evidence

Performance debt.

---

# 167. DV-5 — Reproducibility Evidence

DX/research/tooling debt.

---

# 168. Verification Strength Matches Debt Impact

Architecture/integration debt normally needs:

> DV-3 or stronger.

---

# Technical Debt Invariants

## DEBT-INV-01

Technical debt is a conscious implementation compromise, not missing mandatory work.

## DEBT-INV-02

Risk, bug, blocker, scope gap and technical debt remain distinct.

## DEBT-INV-03

Debt can be accepted only while current capability invariants still pass.

## DEBT-INV-04

Missing F0/F1 capability cannot be classified as debt.

## DEBT-INV-05

Security, authority, Oracle isolation and research-integrity violations cannot be classified as debt.

## DEBT-INV-06

Every material debt has one owner.

## DEBT-INV-07

Every material debt records why it was intentionally accepted.

## DEBT-INV-08

Principal and interest are recorded separately.

## DEBT-INV-09

Every material debt has a LatestCarryMilestone.

## DEBT-INV-10

“When we have time” is not a valid repayment condition.

## DEBT-INV-11

High-interest critical-path debt outranks low-interest cosmetic debt.

## DEBT-INV-12

Architectural debt is treated as high-compounding debt.

## DEBT-INV-13

P-XL architectural debt requires ADR-level review.

## DEBT-INV-14

Contract debt cannot create semantic ambiguity.

## DEBT-INV-15

Critical safety/security test gaps cannot survive their acceptance gate as ordinary test debt.

## DEBT-INV-16

Data debt cannot weaken dataset identity, split integrity or required provenance.

## DEBT-INV-17

Final ML/Vision training cannot depend on undocumented notebook state.

## DEBT-INV-18

Optimization sophistication may carry debt; feasibility may not.

## DEBT-INV-19

Workflow generality may carry debt; workflow safety may not.

## DEBT-INV-20

Platform ergonomics may carry debt; reproducibility/source-of-truth semantics may not.

## DEBT-INV-21

Observability breadth may carry debt; critical diagnosability may not.

## DEBT-INV-22

Performance debt is valid only while accepted hard limits still pass.

## DEBT-INV-23

Research-tooling convenience may carry debt; research validity may not.

## DEBT-INV-24

Intentionally introduced debt should be visible in its originating PR.

## DEBT-INV-25

Material debt cannot exist only as anonymous TODO.

## DEBT-INV-26

Debt budget is interest-weighted rather than count-weighted.

## DEBT-INV-27

Debt saturation may pause new feature work.

## DEBT-INV-28

Debt deadline extensions require explicit review.

## DEBT-INV-29

Repeated deadline extensions trigger architecture/scope reassessment.

## DEBT-INV-30

Debt closes only after appropriate verification.

## DEBT-INV-31

Debt repayment follows normal Git/PR/review workflow.

## DEBT-INV-32

Debt ownership transfers explicitly with capability ownership.

## DEBT-INV-33

Research-critical new debt after M6 is prohibited by default.

## DEBT-INV-34

Final release may retain bounded maintainability debt but no acceptance-invalidating debt.

## DEBT-INV-35

M8 cannot PASS with BREACHED debt affecting F0/F1/R1 acceptance.

---

# Başarı Kriterleri

Madde 71 başarılı uygulanmış sayılabilmek için:

1. Technical Debt ile Scope Gap ayrılmalıdır.
2. Risk/Issue/Blocker/Debt semantics ayrı tutulmalıdır.
3. Technical debt only intentional compromise olarak kullanılmalıdır.
4. Debt qualification gate bulunmalıdır.
5. Debt categories explicit olmalıdır.
6. Security/authority/research-integrity debt category olarak normalleştirilmemelidir.
7. TechnicalDebtRecord first-class olmalıdır.
8. Principal ve interest ayrı tutulmalıdır.
9. Principal size classes tanımlanmalıdır.
10. Interest levels tanımlanmalıdır.
11. Debt lifecycle explicit olmalıdır.
12. BREACHED state bulunmalıdır.
13. CONVERTED state bulunmalıdır.
14. Debt acceptance authority impact’a göre artmalıdır.
15. Significant debt self-accepted olmamalıdır.
16. Every debt LatestCarryMilestone taşımalıdır.
17. POST-PROJECT carry restricted olmalıdır.
18. E2E/M4/M5/M6/M8 debt gates explicit olmalıdır.
19. Missing F0/F1 debt olarak adlandırılamamalıdır.
20. Hard authority/security/Oracle violations debt olamamalıdır.
21. Architectural debt earlier repayment pressure taşımalıdır.
22. Contract debt semantic ambiguity yaratamamalıdır.
23. Critical test debt relevant milestone’dan önce kapanmalıdır.
24. Dataset identity/split/provenance debt’e dönüştürülememelidir.
25. Final ML pipeline notebook-state dependence taşımamalıdır.
26. Scheduler feasibility debt’e dönüştürülememelidir.
27. Workflow safety debt’e dönüştürülememelidir.
28. Platform reproducibility debt’e dönüştürülememelidir.
29. Critical observability/diagnosability debt’e dönüştürülememelidir.
30. Performance debt yalnız hard acceptance boundary içinde geçerli olmalıdır.
31. Normative documentation debt deadline taşımalıdır.
32. Research validity debt’e dönüştürülememelidir.
33. Debt originating PR’da görünür olmalıdır.
34. Material debt yalnız TODO ile takip edilmemelidir.
35. Debt budget interest-weighted olmalıdır.
36. Debt saturation trigger bulunmalıdır.
37. Repayment triggers objective olmalıdır.
38. “When we have time” yasak olmalıdır.
39. Critical debt repayment feature work’ten daha yüksek priority alabilmelidir.
40. Debt repayment normal PR/review workflow izlemelidir.
41. Debt closure verification gerektirmelidir.
42. Speculative over-abstraction debt olarak tanınmalıdır.
43. ScopeDebt yalnız mandatory semantics korunurken geçerli olmalıdır.
44. High-interest debt relevant RiskRecord ile ilişkilendirilmelidir.
45. Debt ownership transfers explicit olmalıdır.
46. FinalResidualDebtRegister üretilmelidir.
47. Deadline extension reviewed olmalıdır.
48. Repeated extension architecture review trigger etmelidir.
49. M6 research-critical debt freeze uygulanmalıdır.
50. EmergencyDebt strict expiry taşımalıdır.
51. M8 BREACHED F0/F1/R1 debt ile PASS edememelidir.

# Açık Sorular

Madde 71 kapsamında core Technical Debt governance’a ilişkin kritik açık soru bulunmamaktadır.

Implementation sırasında refine edilebilecek details:

* exact DebtID naming
* exact dashboard representation
* exact interest scoring heuristics
* exact repayment-trigger thresholds
* exact final residual-debt report format.

Bunlar accepted debt semantics’ini değiştirmeyecektir.

---

# Nihai Karar

Platform Technical Debt governance:

> **Technical debt’i missing scope, bug, blocker, risk ve acceptance failure’dan kesin biçimde ayıran; yalnız mandatory semantics halen geçerliyken conscious implementation compromise olarak kabul eden; every material debt’i Principal, Interest, Owner, RepaymentTrigger, LatestCarryMilestone ve Verification ile bağlayan; architectural/high-interest debt’in erken compound etkisini yöneten; overdue debt’i BREACHED state’e yükselten; M6 öncesi research-critical debt’i kapatan ve final release’de yalnız bounded, documented, acceptance-safe residual maintainability debt’e izin veren debt-management model**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

Ana prensipler:

**Missing Mandatory Capability ≠ Technical Debt**

**Bug ≠ Debt**

**Risk ≠ Debt**

**Hard Invariant Violation ≠ Debt**

**Principal ≠ Interest**

**Every Debt Has an Owner**

**Every Debt Has an Expiry**

**“When We Have Time” Is Not a Plan**

**Architecture Debt Compounds Faster**

**Optimization Sophistication May Be Debt; Feasibility May Not**

**Workflow Generality May Be Debt; Workflow Safety May Not**

**Research Tooling Convenience May Be Debt; Research Validity May Not**

**Debt Count Is Not Quality**

**Debt Repayment Is Real Engineering Work**

**M6 Freezes Research-Critical Debt**

**Final Release May Carry Bounded Debt, Never Acceptance Failure**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

# 72 — Documentation

## Durum

**Approved**

## Amaç

Intelligent Manufacturing Operations Platform for Critical Aerospace Components documentation sistemini yalnız final raporlama faaliyeti olarak değil;

* architecture governance,
* implementation traceability,
* operational reproducibility,
* research reproducibility,
* release integrity,
* team knowledge transfer,
* thesis evidence grounding

için kullanılan version-controlled engineering surface olarak tanımlamak.

Canonical documentation lifecycle:

> **Define Source of Truth → Document Intent → Encode Contracts → Record Decisions → Document Operations → Bind Evidence → Derive Reference Material → Trace Into Thesis → Detect Drift**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

Ana prensipler:

> **A Fact Must Have One Canonical Owner and One Canonical Source of Truth**

> **A Change Is Not Complete Until Affected Normative Documentation Is Updated**

> **Documentation Describes the System That Exists, Not the System the Team Once Intended to Build**

# Documentation Classes

the Manufacturing Operations Platform documentation corpus’u farklı authority seviyelerine sahip artifact classes’a ayrılır.

## 1. NORMATIVE

Sistemin:

* ne yapması gerektiğini,
* hangi boundary’lere sahip olduğunu,
* hangi invariant’ların geçerli olduğunu

tanımlar.

High authority.

---

# 2. DECISION

Architecture/design kararlarının:

* neden alındığını,
* hangi alternatiflerin değerlendirildiğini,
* hangi tradeoff’un kabul edildiğini

kaydeder.

Canonical example:

> ADR.

---

# 3. OPERATIONAL

Sistemin:

* nasıl çalıştırılacağını,
* deploy edileceğini,
* gözlemleneceğini,
* troubleshoot edileceğini,
* recover edileceğini

tanımlar.

Examples:

* runbooks
* deployment guide
* restore guide.

---

# 4. EVIDENCE

Gerçekte:

* ne çalıştırıldığını,
* ne test edildiğini,
* ne ölçüldüğünü,
* hangi release/data/model ile sonuç üretildiğini

kanıtlar.

Examples:

* EvidenceBundle
* ExperimentRun
* BenchmarkRun
* RecoveryTestRun.

---

# 5. REFERENCE / GENERATED

Canonical source’dan türetilen navigation/reference artifacts.

Examples:

* generated OpenAPI docs
* schema indexes
* generated ERD
* CLI reference
* SBOM reports.

---

# 6. THESIS / REPORT

Thesis/report ayrı bir narrative layer’dır.

Canonical engineering source of truth değildir.

Thesis:

> normative + evidence artifacts’tan türetilir.

# Canonical Source-of-Truth Precedence

Different fact classes have different authoritative artifacts.

| Question                       | Canonical Source                                         |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Product vision/scope           | Master Project Specification                             |
| Current architecture           | System Architecture Specification + accepted ADR effects |
| Architecture rationale/history | ADR                                                      |
| Exact API schema               | OpenAPI / executable contract                            |
| Exact event schema             | Versioned event contract                                 |
| Database structure             | Alembic migrations / actual schema                       |
| DB ownership semantics         | Architecture/Data ownership docs                         |
| Workflow logic/version         | Versioned workflow definition                            |
| Runtime nonsecret config       | Git versioned configuration                              |
| Exact deployed composition     | ReleaseManifest                                          |
| Environment observed state     | EnvironmentManifest                                      |
| Exact model version            | ModelPackage / deployment binding                        |
| Dataset identity               | DatasetVersion                                           |
| Dataset split                  | SplitManifest                                            |
| Retrieval configuration        | RetrievalProfile                                         |
| Experiment protocol            | ExperimentDefinition / ProtocolFreeze                    |
| What actually occurred         | Run record / EvidenceBundle                              |
| Recovery steps                 | Runbook                                                  |
| Academic claim                 | Thesis backed by EvidenceRefs                            |

---

# 19. Single Source of Truth Does Not Mean Single File

Each fact category has one canonical artifact.

---

# 20. Code Is Not Sufficient Documentation

Code expresses implementation behavior.

It may not express:

* intent
* rationale
* authority
* claim boundary
* architecture tradeoff.

---

# 21. Prose Does Not Override Executable Contract

When prose and executable schema disagree:

> executable interface contract is authoritative for exact wire semantics.

Prose must be corrected.

---

# 22. ADR Does Not Replace Architecture Specification

ADR answers:

> Why?

Architecture Specification answers:

> What is current?

# 123. Typographical Fixes Do Not Automatically Reopen Freeze

Semantic changes follow normal governance.

---

# Thesis Relationship

## 124. Thesis Does Not Reimplement System Specification

Engineering documentation holds detailed system truth.

Thesis provides academic narrative.

---

# 125. Thesis Covers

* problem
* motivation
* system design
* research methodology
* evaluation
* results
* contribution
* limitations.

---

# 126. Thesis Claims Must Trace to Evidence

Example:

A quantitative performance claim must internally map to:

* ResearchQuestion
* ExperimentDefinition
* AnalysisRun
* EvidenceBundle.

---

# Open-Source Documentation

Internal and public documentation may differ in visibility.

---

# 127. Public Documentation Must Be Truthful but Sanitized

Do not expose:

* secrets
* private hosts/IPs
* restricted artifacts
* inappropriate sensitive operational details.

---

# 128. Public-Safe View Must Not Rewrite Internal Engineering History

Sanitization is controlled publication.

---

# 129. Public Release Redaction Must Be Structured

Madde 78 will finalize open-source publication process.

---

# Documentation Freshness

Critical operational documents should optionally record:

> `LastValidatedAgainstRelease`

rather than only modification date.

---

# 130. Validation Date Matters More Than Edit Date for Runbooks

---

# Documentation Debt

Madde 71 governance applies.

Acceptable:

* optional tutorial backlog.

Unacceptable at relevant milestone:

* incorrect restore guide
* incorrect final benchmark guide
* misleading authority documentation.

---

# Documentation Metrics

Useful indicators:

* broken links
* stale generated docs
* unowned normative docs
* PR documentation-impact compliance
* unexercised runbooks
* requirements missing evidence links
* stale diagrams
* thesis claims without EvidenceRef.

---

# 131. Page Count Is Not a Documentation KPI

---

## 132. One Giant File Containing Everything

Rejected.

Master Spec remains product-level, not operational dumping ground.

# 133. Mutable External Wiki as Sole Source

Rejected.

---

# 134. README-Only Architecture

Rejected.

---

# 135. Repeated Exact Schemas in Multiple Markdown Files

Rejected.

---

# 136. Diagram-Only Critical Semantics

Rejected.

---

# 137. Runbook Without Verification

Rejected.

---

# 138. Screenshot as Sole Evidence

Rejected.

---

# 139. Notebook as Final Research Truth

Rejected.

---

# 140. Thesis as Canonical Product Specification

Rejected.

# 141. “Update Docs at the End”

Rejected.

# Documentation Invariants

## DOC-INV-01

Documentation is a versioned engineering artifact, not final-phase prose work.

## DOC-INV-02

Every material fact has one canonical source of truth.

## DOC-INV-03

Single source of truth means one authoritative artifact per fact rather than one giant file.

## DOC-INV-04

Product scope and product-level invariants belong to Master Specification.

## DOC-INV-05

Current system structure belongs to System Architecture Specification.

## DOC-INV-06

Historical architecture rationale belongs to ADRs.

## DOC-INV-07

Executable interface contracts are canonical for exact API/event structure.

## DOC-INV-08

Database migrations/schema are canonical for exact DB structure.

## DOC-INV-09

ReleaseManifest is canonical for exact deployed composition.

## DOC-INV-10

DatasetVersion/SplitManifest are canonical for dataset identity and split.

## DOC-INV-11

ExperimentDefinition/ProtocolFreeze are canonical for formal experiment behavior.

## DOC-INV-12

EvidenceBundle/Run records are canonical for what actually occurred.

## DOC-INV-13

Runbooks are canonical operational response procedures.

## DOC-INV-14

Thesis derives from engineering/evidence sources and cannot override them.

## DOC-INV-15

Changes invalidating normative docs require same-PR update by default.

## DOC-INV-16

Contract examples validate against actual schema where practical.

## DOC-INV-17

Generated documentation cannot become independent normative truth.

## DOC-INV-18

Generated documentation identifies its generating source.

## DOC-INV-19

Diagrams explain but do not exclusively define critical invariants.

## DOC-INV-20

Normative duplication is minimized.

## DOC-INV-21

Documentation ownership follows capability ownership.

## DOC-INV-22

No teammate becomes universal documentation owner.

## DOC-INV-23

Cross-domain normative documentation receives appropriate cross review.

## DOC-INV-24

Operational runbooks contain explicit verification.

## DOC-INV-25

Critical runbooks are exercised before relevant acceptance gate.

## DOC-INV-26

Notebooks remain exploratory/reference artifacts.

## DOC-INV-27

Final quantitative figures/tables are regenerable from retained evidence.

## DOC-INV-28

Failed/inconclusive experiments remain documented.

## DOC-INV-29

Raw research evidence is immutable while interpretation may evolve.

## DOC-INV-30

Security documentation describes controls without embedding secret values.

## DOC-INV-31

Simulator docs explicitly distinguish operational abstraction from process physics.

## DOC-INV-32

Model/Dataset Cards bound claims to actual evidence domain.

## DOC-INV-33

Stable IDs are preferred over fragile section references.

## DOC-INV-34

Root README is navigation/onboarding surface rather than duplicate specification.

## DOC-INV-35

Broken links and stale generated artifacts are automated checks where practical.

## DOC-INV-36

Documentation debt follows Madde 71 and cannot conceal acceptance failure.

## DOC-INV-37

M6 freezes research-critical documentation semantics.

## DOC-INV-38

M8 documentation corresponds to exact final pinned release.

## DOC-INV-39

Public documentation is sanitized through controlled publication rather than falsifying internal history.

## DOC-INV-40

Documentation quality is judged by correctness, traceability, freshness and reproducibility rather than volume.

Madde 72 başarılı uygulanmış sayılabilmek için:

15. Documentation ownership capability ownership ile align olmalıdır.
16. Universal documentation owner olmamalıdır.
17. Documentation review classes kullanılmalıdır.
18. Same-PR normative update rule uygulanmalıdır.
19. PR template Documentation Impact field taşımalıdır.
20. Delayed material docs changes TD-DOC governance’a girmelidir.

22. Contract docs executable + semantic layers taşımalıdır.
23. Examples schema-validatable olmalıdır.
24. Event Catalog bulunmalıdır.
25. DB prose exact schema duplication yapmamalıdır.
26. AI System Card bulunmalıdır.
27. AI Tool Catalog bulunmalıdır.
28. RAG configuration documentation versioned olmalıdır.
29. Vision Dataset/Model Cards bulunmalıdır.
30. Simulator semantics + assumptions documented olmalıdır.
31. Scheduler constraints/objectives documented olmalıdır.
32. Automation workflow/authority/effect verification documented olmalıdır.
33. Platform operational guides bulunmalıdır.
34. Runbooks trigger→verification lifecycle taşımalıdır.
35. Critical runbooks exercised olmalıdır.
36. ADR and Architecture Spec roles separated olmalıdır.
37. Research artifacts first-class versioned records olmalıdır.
38. Notebook final truth olmamalıdır.
39. Final figures regenerable olmalıdır.
40. Failed/inconclusive runs retained olmalıdır.
41. Generated docs marked/generated-source linked olmalıdır.
42. Architecture diagram families maintained olmalıdır.
43. Diagrams cannot exclusively define critical invariant.
44. Stable IDs used for traceability.
45. Broken links detected olmalıdır.
46. Glossary canonical terminology sağlamalıdır.
47. Onboarding docs non-author tarafından verified olmalıdır.
48. Service Catalog bulunmalıdır.
49. Threat model architecture changes ile evolve etmelidir.
50. Security docs no secrets içermelidir.
51. Model cards claim boundaries göstermelidir.
52. Release docs exact artifact composition’a bağlanmalıdır.

56. Public docs controlled sanitization kullanmalıdır.
57. Operational docs validation/freshness metadata taşımalıdır.
58. Documentation metrics quality odaklı olmalıdır.
59. Page count KPI olmamalıdır.
60. “Docs at the end” workflow rejected olmalıdır.

# Açık Sorular

Madde 72 kapsamında core Documentation architecture’a ilişkin kritik açık soru bulunmamaktadır.

Implementation sırasında refine edilebilecek details:

* exact documentation folder names
* document metadata serialization
* exact link-checker/tooling
* exact generated schema tooling
* exact diagram-as-code syntax
* exact ServiceCatalog format
* exact documentation build pipeline.

Bunlar accepted source-of-truth semantics’i değiştirmeyecektir.

---

# Nihai Karar

Platform Documentation architecture:

> **Documentation’ı NORMATIVE, DECISION, OPERATIONAL, EVIDENCE ve REFERENCE/GENERATED classes’a ayıran; every material fact için tek canonical source-of-truth belirleyen; Master Specification’ı product constitution, Architecture Specification’ı current architecture, ADR’leri decision history, executable schemas’ı exact contract truth, ReleaseManifest’i exact release truth ve EvidenceBundles’ı actual-result truth olarak konumlandıran; normative-impacting code changes için same-PR documentation updates zorunlu kılan; runbooks, model/dataset cards, research artifacts, generated docs, stable IDs ve RTM üzerinden code→contract→decision→operation→evidence→thesis traceability kuran docs-as-engineering governance model**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

Ana prensipler:

**Documentation Is an Engineering Artifact**

**Every Fact Has One Canonical Source**

**Single Source of Truth Does Not Mean One Giant File**

**Architecture Spec = Current State**

**ADR = Decision History**

**Executable Contract = Exact Interface Truth**

**ReleaseManifest = Exact Release Truth**

**EvidenceBundle = What Actually Happened**

**Same Code Change, Same Documentation Change**

**Runbook Must Be Exercised**

**Notebook Is Not Final Evidence**

**Thesis Derives From Engineering Truth**

**Generated Docs Must Not Become Independent Truth**

**Stable IDs Beat Fragile Section References**

**Documentation Quality = Correct + Current + Traceable + Reproducible**

**Page Count Is Not Quality**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.
