# F0 Doctrine

F0 is intentionally sparse.

It identifies capabilities whose removal destroys the the Manufacturing Operations Platform product identity.

Representative F0 anchors include:

* canonical manufacturing domain
* reentrant operational model
* Simulator
* Digital Twin
* versioned integration
* real Vision inspection path
* operational AI/RCA
* Scheduler
* durable Automation
* HITL/authority
* Command Center
* reproducible integrated runtime
* GS-01 real-path integration.

---

# F1 Doctrine

F1 contains mandatory operational depth such as:

* idempotency
* revision protection
* OOD
* calibration
* provenance
* feasibility validation
* effect verification
* observability
* restore
* security
* audit.

F1 is mandatory even though not every F1 item defines product identity by itself.

---

# R1 Doctrine

R1 contains mandatory research/evidence functionality such as:

* experiment runner
* benchmark records
* immutable raw evidence
* final AnalysisPackage
* FinalBenchmarkEvidenceBundle.

R1 failure can prevent M7/M8/research completion even if manufacturing product behavior exists.

---

# Requirement-to-Test Model

Traceability is:

> many-to-many.

One FR may have:

* unit test
* integration test
* E2E
* benchmark
* resilience drill.

One E2E may verify multiple FRs.

Madde 83 shall map these relationships.

---

# Requirement Verification Lifecycle

Canonical:

> **DEFINED → IMPLEMENTED → TESTED → VERIFIED**

---

# IMPLEMENTED

The behavior exists in implementation.

---

# TESTED

Declared verification assets execute against it.

---

# VERIFIED

Required evidence passed against the applicable accepted/final baseline.

---

# 161. Merge Does Not Equal Verification

A merged implementation is not automatically a completed requirement.

---

# Failure Semantics

## F0 Failure

> product identity / product acceptance failure.

## F1 Failure

> final product acceptance failure unless formally rebaselined.

## R1 Failure

> research/evidence completion failure and potentially M7/M8 failure.

---

# Requirement Waivers

Informal final waivers are prohibited.

A failed requirement requires one of:

1. implementation correction,
2. formally approved requirement change,
3. formally approved scope rebaseline,
4. product/research failure disposition.

---

# 162. “Known Limitation” Is Not an Automatic Waiver

If requirement semantics disallow the behavior, limitation text cannot convert FAIL to PASS.

---

# Canonical Requirement Source

The long-form requirement catalog is the normative requirement source.

`03_Requirements_Traceability_Matrix.md` is a traceability index.

It SHALL NOT become a second independently maintained wording source.

---

# 163. RTM References Canonical Requirement Text

Avoid wording drift.

---

# Requirement Milestone Semantics

## M2

Foundational requirement identities stable enough for integrated spine.

## M3

Closed-loop F0 path executable.

## M4

100% F0/F1 implemented.

## M5

100% F0/F1 have executable verification coverage and are evaluation-ready.

## M6

Behavior-affecting requirement semantics frozen for final research.

## M7

Applicable R1 final evidence requirements verified.

## M8

All F0/F1 requirements receive final disposition.

---

# Coverage Gates

## 164. M4 Gate

> 100% F0/F1 requirements have implementation references.

---

# 165. M5 Gate

> 100% F0/F1 requirements have declared verification assets.

---

# 166. M6 Gate

> zero orphan F0/F1 requirements.

---

# 167. M8 Gate

Every F0/F1 requirement is:

> VERIFIED

or explicitly:

> SUPERSEDED by an approved replacement.

No unknown/forgotten requirements remain.

---

# Requirement Quality Rules

Normative FR wording should avoid undefined adjectives such as:

* robust
* fast
* scalable
* user-friendly
* production-grade
* reliable
* intelligent
* secure

unless the statement identifies concrete required behavior.

Quantitative quality belongs to NFRs where appropriate.

---

# Functional Requirement Invariants

## FRC-INV-01

Every mandatory functional requirement has a permanent stable ID.

## FRC-INV-02

Requirement IDs are never recycled.

## FRC-INV-03

Mandatory behavior uses SHALL / SHALL NOT semantics.

## FRC-INV-04

Optional implementation ideas are excluded from the mandatory FR catalog.

## FRC-INV-05

Every F0/F1 requirement has exactly one PrimaryOwner.

## FRC-INV-06

Every F0/F1 requirement traces to an approved source decision.

## FRC-INV-07

Every F0/F1 requirement has a declared verification method.

## FRC-INV-08

Every VERIFIED requirement has acceptance evidence.

## FRC-INV-09

Implementation existence is not equivalent to verification.

## FRC-INV-10

Functional behavior and quantitative quality thresholds remain separated between Madde 81 and Madde 82.

## FRC-INV-11

F0 contains product-identity capabilities rather than every important requirement.

## FRC-INV-12

F1 remains mandatory despite not always defining product identity.

## FRC-INV-13

Mandatory research/evidence functionality uses R1 where appropriate.

## FRC-INV-14

Private cross-service database coupling cannot satisfy an integration requirement.

## FRC-INV-15

AI proposal functionality cannot satisfy mutation/execution requirements.

## FRC-INV-16

Scheduler output cannot satisfy execution eligibility until independent validation passes.

## FRC-INV-17

Command acknowledgement cannot satisfy effect-verification requirements.

## FRC-INV-18

UI rendering cannot substitute for backend authority enforcement.

## FRC-INV-19

Simulator Oracle data cannot satisfy runtime evidence requirements.

## FRC-INV-20

Development mocks cannot satisfy final integrated-boundary requirements unless the requirement explicitly concerns test behavior.

## FRC-INV-21

Formal demo evidence cannot automatically replace formal benchmark evidence.

## FRC-INV-22

One evidence artifact may verify multiple requirements only if every requirement’s acceptance condition remains independently inspectable.

## FRC-INV-23

Every requirement failure receives explicit final disposition.

## FRC-INV-24

Requirement waivers cannot silently bypass product acceptance.

## FRC-INV-25

Semantic requirement changes after M6 receive freeze-impact review.

## FRC-INV-26

Requirements cannot be rewritten after results merely to match observed behavior.

## FRC-INV-27

Final RTM contains no orphan mandatory requirement.

## FRC-INV-28

Final acceptance tests/evidence should trace back to RequirementIDs where applicable.

## FRC-INV-29

Requirement wording cannot imply real-manufacturing-facility capability beyond approved project scope.

## FRC-INV-30

Public/thesis claims cannot exceed capability verified against the catalog.

# 82 — Non-Functional Requirements

## Durum

**Approved**

## Amaç

Intelligent Manufacturing Operations Platform for Critical Aerospace Components için functional correctness’in ötesindeki kalite gereksinimlerini:

* ölçülebilir,
* workload ve hardware context’ine bağlı,
* safety/integrity hard gates ile performance targets’ı ayıran,
* research-scale single-node gerçekliğine uygun,
* final benchmark tarafından doğrulanabilir,
* recovery/reproducibility/evidence kalitesini de kapsayan

bir Non-Functional Requirements baseline’ı olarak tanımlamak.

Canonical lifecycle:

> **Define Quality Attribute → Define Measurement Context → Assign Threshold Class → Freeze Metric → Measure on Declared Hardware/Workload → Preserve Raw Evidence → Evaluate Threshold → Record Residual Risk → Trace to Acceptance**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

Ana prensipler:

> **An NFR Without a Measurement Context Is Only an Adjective**

> **Safety and Integrity Thresholds Are Hard Gates; Performance Numbers Are Hardware- and Workload-Bound**

> **A Single-Node Research Platform Is Evaluated Through Recovery and Resilience Scenarios, Not Fabricated HA Percentages**

> **Measured Characterization Is Better Than an Unsupported SLO**

---

# NFR Record Model

Every NFR SHALL contain:

```text
NFRID
Revision
Title
Statement
QualityClass
PrimaryOwner
MeasurementMetric
MeasurementContext
Threshold
WorkloadProfile
HardwareProfile
VerificationMethod
AcceptanceEvidence
DerivedFrom
Status
```

---

# Stable IDs

Canonical pattern:

```text
NFR-<DOMAIN>-NNN
```

Examples:

```text
NFR-PERF-004
NFR-REL-003
NFR-SEC-001
NFR-REP-002
```

NFRIDs are permanent historical identities.

Retired/superseded IDs are never reused.

---

# Quality Classes

## H0 — HARD

Safety/integrity invariant.

Any failure blocks acceptance.

---

# A1 — ACCEPTANCE

Mandatory quantitative bound.

Must PASS unless formally rebaselined.

---

# S2 — SLO / TARGET

Important engineering target.

Failure requires:

* disclosure
* analysis
* risk/debt/limitation

but does not automatically cause PRODUCT_FAIL.

---

# C3 — CHARACTERIZE

Measurement is mandatory.

No arbitrary pass threshold is imposed before evidence/hardware is known.

---

# Measurement Context

Every quantitative result is bound to:

> **ReleaseManifest + EnvironmentManifest + HardwareProfile + ResourceProfile + WorkloadProfile + BenchmarkDefinition**

where applicable.

A number without its context is not valid final evidence.

---

# Canonical Operational Workload Profiles

## WP-SMALL

Approximately:

> **25 tools / 200 active lots**

Used for:

* small local tests
* development
* fast integration.

---

# WP-NORMAL

Approximately:

> **100 tools / 1,000 active lots**

Canonical normal-scale final operational profile.

---

# WP-STRESS

Approximately:

> **200 tools / 2,000 active lots**

Stress/capacity boundary profile.

These are research-scale operational loads, not claims about real manufacturing facility capacity.

---

# Scheduler Profiles

## SP-NORMAL

Approximately:

> **≤100 eligible lots / ≤50 relevant tools**

---

# SP-STRESS

Approximately:

> **≤250 eligible lots / ≤100 relevant tools**

Stress scheduling is a decision-window benchmark, not full-world monolithic optimization.

---

# Measurement Rules

Latency results SHALL use distributions rather than single fastest runs.

Where appropriate report:

* p50
* p95
* p99.

Formal latency acceptance should use at least:

> **100 observations**

unless BenchmarkDefinition requires more.

Wall-clock timing uses:

> monotonic elapsed time.

Simulation time remains separate.

Human think/approval time remains separate from system-processing time.

---

## NFR-GOV-001 — Stable Identity

**Class:** H0
**Owner:** Asrın

Every mandatory NFR SHALL have a globally unique permanent NFRID.

---

## NFR-GOV-002 — ID Non-Reuse

**Class:** H0
**Owner:** Asrın

Retired or superseded NFRIDs SHALL NOT be reused.

---

## NFR-GOV-003 — Primary Ownership

**Class:** H0
**Owner:** Asrın

Every mandatory NFR SHALL have exactly one PrimaryOwner.

---

## NFR-GOV-004 — Measurement Context

**Class:** H0
**Owner:** Yavuz

Every quantitative NFR SHALL identify its metric and measurement context.

---

## NFR-GOV-005 — Hardware Binding

**Class:** H0
**Owner:** Yavuz

Every hardware-dependent final result SHALL identify HardwareProfile.

---

## NFR-GOV-006 — Load Binding

**Class:** H0
**Owner:** Yavuz

Every load-dependent final result SHALL identify WorkloadProfile or equivalent workload definition.

---

## NFR-GOV-007 — Threshold Class

**Class:** H0
**Owner:** Asrın

Every mandatory NFR SHALL be classified as:

> H0 / A1 / S2 / C3.

---

## NFR-GOV-008 — Freeze Change Control

**Class:** H0
**Owner:** Asrın

Material NFR threshold/semantic changes after M6 SHALL undergo formal freeze-impact/change-control review.

---

## NFR-GOV-009 — Evidence Requirement

**Class:** H0
**Owner:** Yavuz

A final NFR SHALL NOT be marked VERIFIED without durable measurement evidence.

---

## NFR-GOV-010 — No Quality Averaging

**Class:** H0
**Owner:** Asrın

NFR failures SHALL NOT be hidden by averaging unrelated quality attributes into one overall score.

# B. Performance / Latency — `NFR-PERF`

## NFR-PERF-001 — Core/Twin Read Latency

**Class:** S2
**Owner:** Asrın

Under `WP-NORMAL`, common Core/Twin read queries SHOULD achieve:

> **p95 ≤ 500 ms**

from backend/BFF request receipt to response generation.

Browser rendering/network presentation is excluded.

---

## NFR-PERF-002 — Core Command Decision Latency

**Class:** S2
**Owner:** Asrın

Normal domain commands that do not wait for downstream workflow/physical execution SHOULD produce an accepted/rejected result at:

> **p95 ≤ 750 ms**

This measures validation/persistence, not final manufacturing effect.

---

## NFR-PERF-003 — Outbox Publication Delay

**Class:** A1
**Owner:** Asrın

Under `WP-NORMAL`, healthy dependencies:

> committed outbox record → durable broker publication

SHALL achieve:

> **p95 ≤ 2 s**
> **p99 ≤ 5 s**

---

## NFR-PERF-004 — Twin Freshness

**Class:** A1
**Owner:** Asrın

Under `WP-NORMAL` with healthy event backbone:

> canonical event → readable Twin projection

SHALL achieve:

> **p95 ≤ 2 s**
> **p99 ≤ 5 s**

---

## NFR-PERF-005 — Command Center State Visibility

**Class:** S2
**Owner:** Asrın

After backend/Twin state becomes current, primary Command Center views SHOULD reflect the updated state within:

> **p95 ≤ 3 s**

on accepted local/integration network.

---

## NFR-PERF-006 — RAG Retrieval Latency

**Class:** S2
**Owner:** Asrın

For the frozen final corpus and RetrievalProfile:

> top-k retrieval SHOULD achieve p95 ≤ 2 s

excluding downstream LLM generation.

---

## NFR-PERF-007 — AI RCA Latency

**Class:** S2
**Owner:** Asrın

The final RCA path SHOULD normally produce a structured result within:

> **p95 ≤ 60 s**

from orchestrator start.

Declared external-provider outage/retry scenarios are handled separately.

No industrial hard-real-time guarantee is implied.

---

## NFR-PERF-008 — Scheduler Decision Budget

**Class:** A1
**Owner:** Batu

For every `SP-NORMAL` instance, the Scheduler SHALL return either:

* a ScheduleValidator-feasible candidate,
* an accepted fallback,
* or an explicit failure state

within:

> **30 s wall-clock**

---

## NFR-PERF-009 — Vision CPU Smoke Latency

**Class:** A1
**Owner:** Selman

The documented CPU smoke path SHALL process the accepted small inspection sample within:

> **15 s/image**

on the documented CPU baseline.

This is a developer/public-smoke threshold, not final accelerated inference performance.

---

## NFR-PERF-010 — Final Vision Inference Latency

**Class:** C3
**Owner:** Selman

Formal Vision inference SHALL be measured separately for:

* cold start
* warm inference
* CPU/GPU HardwareProfile as applicable.

No universal threshold is imposed before final hardware/model selection.

---

## NFR-PERF-011 — Workflow Control-Plane Overhead

**Class:** S2
**Owner:** Batu

For protected actions that do not require long deliberate physical/simulation waits:

> authorization-ready workflow step → verified Core/Twin effect

SHOULD add:

> **p95 ≤ 10 s**

of system-controlled workflow overhead.

Human wait is excluded.

---

## NFR-PERF-012 — Approval Persistence Latency

**Class:** S2
**Owner:** Yavuz

Authenticated approve/reject submission → durable approval record SHOULD achieve:

> **p95 ≤ 2 s**

on Integration/Evaluation profile.

---

## NFR-PERF-013 — GS-01 System-Controlled Duration

**Class:** S2
**Owner:** Batu

For the final hero scenario:

> inspection evidence available → verified final recovery state

SHOULD complete within:

> **p95 ≤ 120 s**

excluding:

* human think time
* deliberate simulation waits
* declared provider outage.

---

## NFR-PERF-014 — Command Center Initial Actionable Load

**Class:** S2
**Owner:** Asrın

On the accepted LAN/client profile, the primary Command Center route SHOULD become actionable at:

> **p95 ≤ 3 s**

after warm application startup.

---

# C. Capacity / Throughput — `NFR-CAP`

## NFR-CAP-001 — Normal Operational World

**Class:** A1
**Owner:** Batu

Core + Simulator + Twin SHALL support at least:

> **100 tools and 1,000 active lots**

under `WP-NORMAL` without semantic degradation.

---

## NFR-CAP-002 — Stress Operational World

**Class:** A1
**Owner:** Batu

The system SHALL execute a controlled:

> **200-tool / 2,000-active-lot**

`WP-STRESS` scenario without:

* canonical data corruption
* cross-world leakage
* scale-induced invalid state transition
* OOM failure.

Performance degradation is characterized separately.

---

## NFR-CAP-003 — Simulator Event Volume

**Class:** A1
**Owner:** Batu

The Simulator SHALL process at least:

> **250,000 discrete events**

in the defined stress benchmark without correctness failure.

---

## NFR-CAP-004 — Event Backbone Sustained Load

**Class:** A1
**Owner:** Yavuz

The integrated application event pipeline SHALL sustain:

> **100 durable application messages/s for 10 minutes**

without:

* message loss of committed durable work
* duplicate protected effects.

This benchmarks the application pipeline, not NATS theoretical throughput.

---

## NFR-CAP-005 — Core Command Throughput

**Class:** S2
**Owner:** Asrın

Under controlled synthetic load, the Core SHOULD sustain:

> **20 domain commands/s for 5 minutes**

without correctness failure.

---

## NFR-CAP-006 — Scheduler Normal Capacity

**Class:** A1
**Owner:** Batu

For:

> **≤100 eligible lots / ≤50 relevant tools**

the Scheduler SHALL satisfy `NFR-PERF-008`.

---

## NFR-CAP-007 — Scheduler Stress Frontier

**Class:** C3
**Owner:** Batu

For:

> **≤250 eligible lots / ≤100 relevant tools**

the final benchmark SHALL characterize:

* feasibility rate
* solve time
* solution quality
* fallback rate.

---

## NFR-CAP-008 — Workflow Concurrency

**Class:** A1
**Owner:** Batu

The runtime SHALL sustain:

> **50 simultaneously active/waiting workflows**

without lost workflow state or duplicate protected effects.

---

## NFR-CAP-009 — Interactive User Concurrency

**Class:** S2
**Owner:** Yavuz

The Command Center SHOULD support at least:

> **8 concurrent authenticated interactive sessions**

on the Integration profile without correctness degradation.

---

## NFR-CAP-010 — Isolated World Capacity

**Class:** S2
**Owner:** Yavuz

The Integration/Evaluation runtime SHOULD support at least:

> **5 simultaneously existing isolated WorldIDs**

without cross-world leakage.

They need not all run maximum stress load concurrently.

---

# D. Reliability / Resilience — `NFR-REL`

## NFR-REL-001 — Duplicate Effect Tolerance

**Class:** H0
**Owner:** Batu

Across duplicate-delivery, retry and workflow-restart tests:

> **duplicate protected manufacturing effects = 0**

---

## NFR-REL-002 — Stale / Replay Execution Tolerance

**Class:** H0
**Owner:** Asrın

Across the final authority suite:

> **accepted stale/replayed/mismatched protected executions = 0**

---

## NFR-REL-003 — Stateless Service Restart

# Availability Doctrine

the Manufacturing Operations Platform v1.0 SHALL NOT claim arbitrary:

> 99.9% / 99.99% availability

as a product NFR.

Reason:

* single Integration host
* no HA architecture
* academic/research platform
* insufficient meaningful continuous-production observation window.

Reliability is instead validated through:

* restart
* broker outage
* host reboot
* soak
* recovery
* restore
* duplicate-effect prevention
* degraded-state visibility.

---

# Real-Time Doctrine

the Manufacturing Operations Platform SHALL NOT make a blanket:

> hard real-time system

claim.

Acceptable description:

> **near-real-time operational decision-support/control platform**

within measured latency envelopes.

No deterministic industrial hard-real-time certification is claimed.

---

# Hard-Gate Matrix

The following failures cannot be averaged away:

| Area            | Hard Failure                                       |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Authority       | unauthorized protected action accepted             |
| Idempotency     | duplicate protected effect                         |
| Oracle          | hidden truth available to runtime decision path    |
| Data            | final split leakage                                |
| Security        | known live secret in release                       |
| Evidence        | planned final runs disappear without disposition   |
| Recovery        | final mandatory restore drill fails                |
| Reproducibility | final baseline cannot be reconstructed             |
| Core/Twin       | verified effect remains semantically contradictory |
| Scheduler       | infeasible plan reaches execution eligibility      |

---

# S2 Miss Semantics

An S2 target miss does not automatically cause PRODUCT_FAIL.

It SHALL cause:

> measurement retained → root cause analyzed → risk/debt/limitation recorded → external claim wording updated.

S2 misses cannot be silently called PASS.

---

# C3 Characterization Semantics

C3 requirements still require measurement.

Typical C3 examples:

* final Vision hardware latency
* Scheduler stress frontier
* external LLM variability
* CPU saturation frontier.

Lack of threshold does not mean lack of evidence.

---

# NFR and Final Benchmark

Final NFR evidence SHALL be integrated into FBC-01 where applicable.

Examples:

```text
NFR-PERF-* → performance benchmark
NFR-REL-*  → resilience scenarios
NFR-REC-*  → restore/recovery drills
NFR-SEC-*  → authority/security negative suite
NFR-REP-*  → reproduction run
NFR-DATA-* → final benchmark evidence audit
```

NFR validation is therefore not a detached final-week checklist.

---

# NFR Verification Lifecycle

Canonical state:

> **DEFINED → MEASURABLE → IMPLEMENTED → MEASURED → VERIFIED**

---

# DEFINED

Quality property exists normatively.

---

# MEASURABLE

Metric, context and threshold/class are defined.

---

# IMPLEMENTED

System capabilities required for measurement exist.

---

# MEASURED

Formal evidence has been collected.

---

# VERIFIED

Applicable H0/A1/S2/C3 semantics have been correctly evaluated and recorded.

---

# Milestone NFR Gates

## M3

Hard closed-loop safety/integrity instrumentation exists.

## M4

All mandatory NFRs have measurement strategy.

## M5

Performance/resilience/security/recovery suites are operational.

## M6

All final NFR semantics/thresholds are frozen.

No orphan NFR remains.

## M7

FBC produces final quantitative/reliability evidence.

## M8

Every NFR has final disposition.

---

# Final Acceptance Semantics

At M8:

## H0

> **100% must PASS.**

Any failure blocks product acceptance.

---

# A1

> **100% must PASS**

unless formally rebaselined through approved change control.

---

# S2

Must be:

* measured
* reported
* PASS/MISS explicitly recorded.

Miss does not automatically fail product.

---

# C3

Must be:

* measured
* characterized
* retained in final evidence.

---

# Unknown NFRs

At final acceptance:

> **No H0 or A1 may remain UNKNOWN.**

Unknown mandatory requirement means incomplete acceptance.

---

# Environment Substitution

An NFR bound to the accepted 16 GiB shared host does not PASS because it succeeded on a larger unrelated workstation.

It must be:

* measured in the proper HardwareProfile
* or formally rebaselined.

---

# Regression Review

After M5, selected critical quality metrics receive regression review.

Representative metrics:

* Twin freshness
* event lag
* Scheduler solve time
* E2E duration
* memory.

Approximate:

> **>20% adverse regression**

against accepted comparable baseline triggers investigation.

This is a review trigger, not a universal PRODUCT_FAIL threshold.

---

# Resource Priority

Canonical optimization priority remains:

> **Correctness → Authority/Security → Durability → Reproducibility → Performance**

Performance improvements SHALL NOT weaken:

* idempotency
* audit
* authorization
* evidence integrity
* recoverability.

---

Audit and observability remain distinct.

## NFR-INV-33

Missing mandatory telemetry/evidence may invalidate a formal run.

## NFR-INV-34

Observability overhead is measured.

## NFR-INV-35

Deterministic components require deterministic reproduction.

## NFR-INV-36

Stochastic LLM behavior uses protocol/statistical reproducibility.

## NFR-INV-37

Formal deployments use immutable artifact identities.

## NFR-INV-38

Non-owner reproduction is part of final acceptance.

## NFR-INV-39

Mandatory runtime fits the accepted 16 GiB host envelope.

## NFR-INV-40

Normal operation preserves host resource headroom.

## NFR-INV-41

Formal benchmark/demo forbids undeclared heavy background workloads.

## NFR-INV-42

Storage growth is bounded.

## NFR-INV-43

Core reproduction does not require GPU.

## NFR-INV-44

Kubernetes/cloud are not required for v1 acceptance.

## NFR-INV-45

DX targets cannot bypass security/architecture semantics.

## NFR-INV-46

Release gates cannot rely on retry-until-green flakiness.

## NFR-INV-47

Critical documentation commands are validated.

## NFR-INV-48

Dataset/evidence provenance completeness is quantitative.

## NFR-INV-49

Final split leakage has zero tolerance.

## NFR-INV-50

Every planned final experimental unit receives an auditable disposition.

## NFR-INV-51

Critical UI state cannot rely on color alone.

## NFR-INV-52

Known stale operational state is visibly marked stale.

## NFR-INV-53

Protected approvals expose sufficient decision context.

## NFR-INV-54

Presenter Mode cannot conceal semantic failure.

## NFR-INV-55

NFR changes after M6 require freeze-impact review.

## NFR-INV-56

NFRs cannot be rewritten after results merely to turn failure into PASS.

## NFR-INV-57

Final acceptance has no UNKNOWN H0/A1 NFR.

## NFR-INV-58

S2 misses are disclosed rather than silently treated as passes.

## NFR-INV-59

C3 requirements still require measurement evidence.

## NFR-INV-60

Public/thesis/portfolio quality claims cannot exceed final NFR evidence.

# Açık Sorular

Madde 82 kapsamında core Non-Functional Requirements architecture’a ilişkin kritik açık soru bulunmamaktadır.

M6/FBC preparation sırasında exact implementation evidence ile refine edilebilecek controlled details:

* exact normal developer HardwareProfile
* final GPU Vision HardwareProfile
* exact latency BenchmarkDefinition sampling/warmup
* exact stress scenario composition
* exact resource-measurement collection method
* exact browser version numbers
* exact compatible DR replacement hardware
* final S2 regression baselines.

Bu details accepted threshold/governance semantics’ini değiştirmeyecektir.

---

# Nihai Karar

Platform Non-Functional Requirements baseline:

> **120 stable-ID quality requirements; H0/A1/S2/C3 threshold classes; explicit workload/hardware contexts; quantified 100-tool/1,000-lot normal and 200-tool/2,000-lot stress profiles; bounded Twin/event/Scheduler/workflow latencies; zero-tolerance authority/idempotency/Oracle/data-integrity gates; scenario-based resilience instead of fake HA; measurable RPO/RTO/reconstruction; zero-secret/Critical-vulnerability security gates; OTel evidence and auditability; deterministic reproducibility; 16 GiB resource envelope; deployability/DX/data-integrity/usability constraints; and FBC-integrated final measurement governance**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

Ana prensipler:

**Quality Without Measurement Context Is Not an NFR**

**Safety and Integrity Are Hard Gates**

**Performance Is Context-Bound**

**No Fake HA**

**No Blanket Hard Real-Time Claim**

**100 Tools / 1,000 Lots Is the Normal Research Profile**

**200 Tools / 2,000 Lots Is the Stress Profile**

**Scheduler NORMAL Must Resolve Within 30 Seconds**

**Twin Freshness Is Explicitly Bounded**

**Duplicate Effects = Zero**

**Stale / Replayed Protected Execution = Zero**

**Recovery Is Measured**

**Backups Must Restore**

**Final Evidence Must Survive Host Loss**

**Known Live Secrets = Zero**

**Final Split Leakage = Zero**

**Every Planned Benchmark Unit Is Accounted For**

**16 GiB Means 16 GiB**

**Core Product Does Not Require GPU**

**Observability Has Its Own Overhead Budget**

**Implemented ≠ Measured ≠ Verified**

**S2 Misses Are Disclosed**

**C3 Still Requires Evidence**

**No H0/A1 Requirement Remains Unknown at M8**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

# 83 — Requirements Traceability Matrix

## Durum

**Approved**

## Amaç

Intelligent Manufacturing Operations Platform for Critical Aerospace Components için toplam:

> **186 Functional Requirement + 120 Non-Functional Requirement = 306 normative requirement**

üzerinden;

* requirement’ın kaynağını,
* architecture allocation’ını,
* implementation artifact’larını,
* executable verification asset’larını,
* actual execution run’larını,
* immutable acceptance evidence’ını,
* research/public claim bağlantılarını,
* risk/debt etkilerini

uçtan uca izleyebilen, machine-readable ve insan tarafından incelenebilir bir traceability system tanımlamak.

Canonical trace chain:

> **Requirement → Source Decision → Architecture Allocation → Implementation → Verification Asset → Execution → Evidence → Acceptance Disposition → Claim**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

Ana prensipler:

> **Traceability Is a Graph; the Matrix Is a Generated View**

> **The RTM Traces Normative Truth; It Does Not Duplicate or Redefine It**

> **No Mandatory Requirement May Be Orphaned, and No Final Claim May Depend on Orphan Evidence**

> **A Green Test Without a RequirementID Is Useful Engineering Evidence but Not Automatically Acceptance Traceability**

> **Evidence Becomes Stale When the Behavior It Proved Materially Changes**

---

# Canonical RTM Role

## 1. Human-Readable Artifact

Canonical human-facing artifact:

> `03_Requirements_Traceability_Matrix.md`

olacaktır.

Bu dosya:

* traceability overview,
* coverage,
* status,
* blockers,
* final acceptance

için generated report olacaktır.

---

# 2. RTM Is Not the Normative Requirement Source

Canonical requirement wording remains in:

* Madde 81 Functional Requirements Catalog
* Madde 82 Non-Functional Requirements Catalog.

RTM SHALL reference RequirementIDs.

It SHALL NOT maintain independently editable duplicate requirement wording.

---

# Source-of-Truth Separation

Canonical truth distribution:

| Fact                  | Canonical Source                |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Requirement semantics | FR/NFR catalogs                 |
| Current architecture  | Architecture Specification      |
| Decision rationale    | ADR                             |
| API/event schema      | Executable contract             |
| Implementation        | Repository                      |
| Verification intent   | Test/Benchmark/Drill definition |
| Actual execution      | Run record                      |
| Acceptance proof      | EvidenceBundle                  |
| Research claim        | ThesisClaimRegister             |
| Trace relationship    | Trace registry                  |

---

# Machine-Readable Trace Registry

The traceability system SHALL maintain a machine-readable relation registry.

Conceptual structure:

```text
traceability/
    trace_edges.yaml
    trace_schema.json
    generated/
        requirements.csv
        verification_coverage.csv
        evidence_coverage.csv
        claim_coverage.csv
        orphan_report.json
```

Exact serialization may change through implementation without changing accepted semantics.

---

# 3. Long-Form Requirement Text Is Not Copied Into the Trace Registry

Example:

```text
FR-CORE-005
```

is referenced by identity.

Its full SHALL statement remains canonical in Madde 81.

---

# Trace Graph Node Types

Canonical node classes:

## 4. `REQ`

Requirement.

Examples:

```text
FR-CORE-005
NFR-REL-001
```

---

# 5. `DEC`

Approved source decision or invariant.

Examples:

```text
ITEM-23
AUTO-INV-08
BENCH-INV-025
```

---

# 6. `ARCH`

Architecture capability/component.

Examples:

```text
ARCH-CORE
ARCH-TWIN
ARCH-VISION
ARCH-SCHEDULER
ARCH-AUTOMATION
```

---

# 7. `ADR`

Architecture Decision Record.

---

# 8. `CONTRACT`

Versioned executable boundary definition.

Examples:

* API operation
* command schema
* event schema
* workflow contract.

---

# 9. `IMPL`

Implementation unit.

Examples:

* service
* package
* module
* workflow definition
* migration
* platform definition.

---

# 10. `DATA`

Dataset, CorpusVersion or SplitManifest artifact.

---

# 11. `MODEL`

ModelPackage or final model binding.

---

# 12. `POLICY`

Examples:

* AuthorityPolicy
* SchedulerPolicy
* RetrievalProfile
* runtime policy.

---

# 13. `SCENARIO`

Executable domain/integration scenario.

---

# 14. `TEST`

Automated verification asset.

---

# 15. `BENCH`

Formal benchmark/ExperimentDefinition.

---

# 16. `DRILL`

Resilience, restore, security or operational drill.

---

# 17. `RUN`

Actual:

* TestRun
* BenchmarkRun
* DemoRun
* RestoreTestRun
* ResilienceRun.

---

# 18. `EVID`

Immutable EvidenceBundle or final result artifact.

---

# 19. `CLAIM`

Major:

* ThesisClaim
* approved PortfolioClaim
* public technical claim.

---

# 20. `RISK`

RiskRecord.

---

# 21. `DEBT`

TechnicalDebtRecord.

---

# 22. Node Requirements Are Context-Sensitive

Not every RequirementID SHALL connect to every node class.

Trace completeness is evaluated according to requirement type.

---

# Controlled Trace Relations

Canonical relation vocabulary:

## 23. `DERIVED_FROM`

Requirement → approved decision/invariant.

---

# 24. `ALLOCATED_TO`

Requirement → architecture capability/component.

---

# 25. `DECIDED_BY`

Requirement/component → relevant ADR.

---

# 26. `EXPOSED_BY`

Requirement → versioned API/event/command/workflow contract.

---

# 27. `REALIZED_BY`

Requirement → implementation artifact.

---

# 28. `USES_DATA`

Requirement/evaluation → DatasetVersion, CorpusVersion or SplitManifest.

---

# 29. `USES_MODEL`

Requirement/evaluation → ModelPackage.

---

# 30. `GOVERNED_BY`

Requirement → policy/configuration artifact.

---

# 31. `EXERCISED_IN`

Requirement → executable scenario.

---

# 32. `VERIFIED_BY`

Requirement → TestID, benchmark or drill.

---

# 33. `EXECUTED_AS`

Verification definition → actual Run.

---

# 34. `EVIDENCED_BY`

Requirement or Run → EvidenceBundle.

---

# 35. `SUPPORTS_CLAIM`

Evidence → major Thesis/Public/Portfolio claim.

---

# 36. `MITIGATES`

Requirement/test/control → RiskRecord.

---

# 37. `CARRIES_DEBT`

Requirement/implementation → legitimate TechnicalDebtRecord.

---

# 38. Relation Vocabulary Is Controlled

Arbitrary relationships such as:

* related_to
* sort_of_checks
* maybe_supports

are prohibited.

---

# TraceEdge Model

Canonical conceptual record:

```text
FromID
Relation
ToID
Applicability
IntroducedIn
LastValidatedIn
Notes
```

Logical edge identity is:

> **FromID + Relation + ToID**

---

# 39. Trace Edges Do Not Need Independent Random UUIDs

Stable engineering artifact IDs plus Git history are sufficient.

Avoid unnecessary bureaucracy.

---

# Artifact Identity Namespaces

Recommended stable namespaces:

```text
ARCH-*
ADR-*
API-*
CMD-*
EVT-*
WF-*
POL-*
DATASET-*
SPLIT-*
CORPUS-*
MODEL-*
SCEN-*
TEST-*
BENCH-*
RES-*
RESTORE-*
DEMO-*
RUN-*
EVID-*
CLAIM-*
RISK-*
TD-*
```

---

# TestID Standard

Acceptance-relevant verification assets SHALL use stable semantic TestIDs.

Canonical family:

```text
TEST-<DOMAIN>-NNN
```

Examples:

```text
TEST-CORE-014
TEST-VIS-027
TEST-AUTH-018
TEST-EVT-011
```

Specialized formal identities may retain semantic names:

```text
E2E-01
BENCH-RQ1-001
BENCH-RQ2-001
RES-BROKER-001
RESTORE-HOST-001
DEMO-GS01-001
```

---

# 40. Global TestID Does Not Equal Individual Test Function

One TestID may represent:

* one test
* parameterized test family
* one acceptance-oriented suite.

Individual helper tests do not require global TestIDs.

---

# Verification Granularity

Traceability focuses on behaviorally meaningful verification assets.

Example:

```text
TEST-AUTO-RESTART-001
```

may contain cases for:

* worker crash
* restart before command
* duplicate delivery
* restart after effect
* restart before effect verification.

---

# Forward Traceability

Canonical forward trace:

> **Requirement → Architecture → Implementation → Verification → Evidence**

For final claims:

> **Requirement → … → Evidence → Claim**

---

# 41. F0/F1 Minimum Forward Trace

At final acceptance every active F0/F1 SHALL have:

1. at least one `DERIVED_FROM`
2. at least one `ALLOCATED_TO`
3. at least one `REALIZED_BY`
4. at least one `VERIFIED_BY`
5. at least one valid final `EVIDENCED_BY` path.

---

# 42. R1 Minimum Forward Trace

Every R1 SHALL have:

* source decision
* implementation/procedure
* verification mechanism
* final research evidence.

---

# 43. NFR Minimum Forward Trace

Every mandatory NFR SHALL trace to:

* approved source
* responsible architecture/operational surface
* measurement/Test/Benchmark/Drill definition
* final measurement evidence.

---

# Backward Traceability

RTM SHALL also answer:

> Why does this implementation exist?

> Why is this test required?

> Which requirement does this evidence prove?

> Which evidence supports this claim?

---

# 44. Acceptance-Critical Verification Must Trace Back

Every acceptance-relevant TestID/Benchmark/Drill SHALL map to one or more:

* FR
* NFR
* accepted invariant.

No unexplained mandatory release gate.

---

# 45. Final Evidence Must Trace Back

Every final EvidenceBundle SHALL identify the verification intent and requirement/evaluation purpose it supports.

---

# 46. Major Claims Must Trace to Evidence

Final major empirical/system claims SHALL identify evidence.

They do not need to map directly to only one RequirementID.

---

# 47. Not Every Source File Requires Requirement Mapping

Implementation mapping is performed at useful semantic granularity:

* service
* package
* bounded-context module
* workflow
* policy
* migration
* platform definition.

Helper files/functions do not require trace records.

---

# Orphan Definitions

## 48. `ORPHAN-REQ`

Mandatory requirement missing required downstream trace.

---

# 49. `ORPHAN-TEST`

Acceptance-critical verification artifact without requirement/invariant trace.

---

# 50. `ORPHAN-EVID`

Final evidence artifact with no accepted verification/research purpose.

---

# 51. `ORPHAN-CLAIM`

Major thesis/public claim lacking valid EvidenceRef.

---

# 52. `ORPHAN-IMPL`

Material standalone implementation capability with no requirement/architecture rationale.

Only meaningful architectural implementation is subject to this rule.

---

# Final Orphan Gates

At M8:

> **active mandatory ORPHAN-REQ = 0**

> **acceptance-critical ORPHAN-TEST = 0**

> **final ORPHAN-EVID = 0**

> **major ORPHAN-CLAIM = 0**

---

# RTM Coverage States

Generated per requirement:

## 53. `UNALLOCATED`

Architecture allocation missing.

## 54. `ALLOCATED`

Architecture surface exists.

## 55. `IMPLEMENTED`

Implementation references exist.

## 56. `VERIFY_PLANNED`

Verification asset exists.

## 57. `EVIDENCE_PENDING`

Verification exists but acceptable final evidence does not yet exist.

## 58. `VERIFIED`

Sufficient current evidence satisfies the requirement.

## 59. `FAILED`

Required verification failed.

## 60. `STALE`

Prior evidence exists but no longer proves current applicable baseline.

## 61. `SUPERSEDED`

Requirement is historical and no longer active.

---

# 62. RTM Coverage State Is a Derived View

It does not replace the canonical requirement lifecycle defined by Madde 81/82.

---

# Evidence Sufficiency

## 63. Verification Sufficiency Is Requirement-Specific

A green unit test is not automatically sufficient.

---

# 64. Real-Boundary Requirements Need Real-Boundary Evidence

Example:

`FR-VIS-016`

cannot be finally verified by mocked Vision output.

It requires actual Vision evidence entering the closed loop.

---

# 65. Local Deterministic Requirements May Be Fully Verified Locally

Examples:

* schema rejection
* state-transition rule
* deterministic validation helper.

No mandatory E2E inflation where unnecessary.

---

# 66. H0 Requires Hard/Negative Evidence

If requirement is:

> unauthorized protected actions = zero,

happy-path evidence is insufficient.

---

# 67. A1 Quantitative Requirements Require Correct Context

Wrong:

* HardwareProfile
* WorkloadProfile
* Environment

does not satisfy context-bound A1.

---

# 68. S2 MISS Is Valid Evidence

An S2 target may have:

> valid evidence + MISS.

MISS is not trace failure.

---

# 69. C3 Still Requires Evidence

Characterization requirement without measurement remains incomplete.

---

# Evidence Environment Classes

Canonical:

> **DEV
> CI
> INTEGRATION
> EVALUATION
> DEMO
> PUBLIC_REPRO**

---

# 70. Evidence Class Matters

DEMO evidence does not automatically satisfy EVALUATION requirements.

DEV evidence does not automatically satisfy formal Integration requirements.

---

# 71. EVALUATION Is Preferred for Final Quantitative Research Claims

---

# Evidence Compatibility

Evidence applicability SHALL consider where relevant:

* release
* Git SHA
* model
* corpus
* dataset/split
* workflow
* policy
* contract
* environment
* HardwareProfile
* WorkloadProfile
* scenario.

---

# 72. Material Behavior Change Can Make Evidence STALE

Example:

workflow retry behavior changes materially.

Old restart evidence becomes:

> STALE.

---

# 73. Documentation-Only Change Does Not Automatically Stale Evidence

Staleness is semantic.

---

# 74. ModelPackage Change Can Stale Model Evaluation

---

# 75. Corpus/RetrievalProfile Change Can Stale RCA/RAG Evidence

---

# 76. SchedulerPolicy Change Can Stale Scheduling Evidence

---

# 77. WorkflowBundle/AuthorityPolicy Change Can Stale Automation/authority Evidence

---

# 78. Hardware Change Can Stale Performance Comparability

It need not stale unrelated functional correctness evidence.

---

# 79. Requirement Semantic Change Normally Stales Prior Evidence

Unless explicit compatibility review proves otherwise.

---

# EvidenceApplicability Model

Suggested conceptual record:

```text
EvidenceID
RequirementID
ReleaseRef
EnvironmentRef
HardwareProfileRef
WorkloadProfileRef
ApplicabilityStatus
```

Statuses:

> **CURRENT
> STALE
> SUPERSEDED
> NOT_APPLICABLE**

---

# Architecture Allocation View

Generated view:

> Requirement → Architecture component(s)

Example:

| Requirement | Architecture                              |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| FR-AI-004   | AI Orchestrator + Core Authority Boundary |
| FR-SCH-005  | Scheduler + ScheduleValidator             |
| FR-AUTO-008 | Automation + Core + Twin                  |
| NFR-REL-006 | NATS + Outbox/Consumers + Platform        |

---

# 80. Cross-Cutting Allocation May Be Many-to-Many

A requirement may map to multiple architecture surfaces.

It still has exactly one PrimaryOwner.

---

# Implementation Coverage View

Generated view:

> Requirement → repo/module/workflow/config.

Example:

```text
FR-CORE-005
    → apps/core/
    → packages/idempotency/
```

---

# 81. Implementation Mapping Is Not Verification

Presence of source code is not acceptance proof.

---

# Contract Trace View

Cross-service requirements SHOULD reference stable versioned contracts.

Examples:

```text
FR-VIS-009
    → EVT-InspectionObservation-v1

FR-SCH-008
    → CONTRACT-RecoveryPlan-v1

FR-AUTO-010
    → CMD-PlaceLotOnHold-v1
```

---

# 82. Contract Identity Is Semantic

Do not trace merely to:

> `events.py`.

---

# ADR Trace View

Material architectural requirements may trace to relevant ADR.

Examples:

* NATS
* Temporal
* Qdrant
* Compose
* PostgreSQL.

---

# 83. ADR Is Rationale, Not Verification

`DECIDED_BY` SHALL NOT satisfy `VERIFIED_BY`.

---

# Scenario Traceability

Every canonical integration scenario SHALL declare which RequirementIDs it exercises.

---

# 84. Scenario Requirement Coverage Does Not Encode Expected Answers

Scenario metadata defines capability coverage.

Evaluator owns expected truth.

---

# GS-01 Trace View

A dedicated generated:

> **GS-01 Trace**

SHALL show:

> Artifact → Vision → InspectionObservation → RCA → Proposal → Scheduler → ScheduleValidator → Approval → Temporal → Core → Simulator → Twin → UI/Audit

with the relevant FR/NFR IDs.

---

# 85. GS-01 Does Not Verify All Requirements

GS-01 proves the integrated product spine.

Specialized:

* security
* restore
* capacity
* OOD
* benchmark
* failure

requirements require their own evidence.

---

# F0 E2E Coverage

Madde 84 SHALL consume a generated:

> **F0 E2E Coverage View**

showing:

* F0 RequirementID
* integrated scenario(s)
* component chain
* evidence.

---

# 86. Every F0 Must Appear in at Least One Real Integrated Acceptance Path

Unit/component-only verification cannot fully satisfy final F0 acceptance.

---

# NFR Trace Views

Dedicated generated views include:

## 87. Performance View

> NFR → BenchmarkDefinition → HardwareProfile → WorkloadProfile → Run → observed result.

## 88. Reliability View

> NFR → ResilienceScenario → Run → recovery result.

## 89. Security View

> NFR → negative/security test → evidence/audit.

## 90. Recoverability View

> NFR → RestoreTestRun → application validation.

## 91. Reproducibility View

> NFR → reproduction execution → evidence.

---

# Quantitative NFR Presentation

Generated RTM SHALL show threshold and observation.

Example:

```text
NFR-PERF-004
Threshold: p95 ≤ 2 s; p99 ≤ 5 s
Observed: p95 1.31 s; p99 3.88 s
Disposition: PASS
Evidence: EVID-PERF-017
```

---

# 92. S2 Misses Remain Explicit

Example:

```text
NFR-PERF-007
Target: p95 ≤ 60 s
Observed: 71.4 s
Disposition: MISS
ProductGate: non-blocking
```

No cosmetic PASS.

---

# Claim Traceability

The `ThesisClaimRegister` SHALL connect to final evidence.

Canonical direction:

> Claim ← Evidence ← Benchmark/Run ← Requirements/System Capability.

---

# 93. Implementation Cannot Directly Prove an Empirical Claim

Code proves implementation existence.

Experiment evidence proves outcome.

---

# 94. Literature Is Not Platform Empirical Evidence

Literature supports:

* background
* methodology
* comparison context.

It does not prove the Manufacturing Operations Platform measured results.

---

# Portfolio / Public Trace

Approved final public metrics/technical claims SHOULD trace through:

> PortfolioMetricExport → final evidence.

The RTM does not need to contain every CV sentence.

---

# 95. RTM Is Not a Marketing Copy Database

---

# Risk Traceability

P0/P1 risks materially affecting requirements SHOULD link to RequirementIDs.

Example:

> authority replay risk → FR-HITL-006 + NFR-SEC-004.

---

# 96. Risk Mitigation Is Not Verification

Mitigation control cannot replace required acceptance evidence.

---

# Technical Debt Traceability

Permitted debt may link to affected requirement.

Example:

> S2 performance miss → TD-PERF-*.

---

# 97. Technical Debt Cannot Normalize H0/A1 Failure

`CARRIES_DEBT` cannot convert a blocking failure to PASS.

---

# PR Requirement Impact

Every material behavior-changing PR SHALL declare:

```text
ImpactedRequirementIDs:
- FR-...
- NFR-...
```

or:

```text
NONE — <reason>
```

---

# 98. Requirement Impact Is Reviewable Metadata

CI validates ID correctness.

Human review validates semantic completeness.

---

# 99. Material Behavioral PR With `NONE` Requires Explicit Reviewer Acceptance

---

# Contract Change Impact

Material API/event/schema change SHALL declare:

* impacted requirements
* affected consumers
* updated verification.

---

# 100. Breaking Contract Change Triggers Evidence-Staleness Review

Prior evidence cannot remain CURRENT automatically.

---

# CODEOWNERS Integration

Trace changes SHALL follow capability ownership.

Examples:

* Asrın-owned requirement mapping → Asrın review
* Selman Vision mappings → Selman
* Batu planning/workflow mappings → Batu
* Yavuz platform/runtime mappings → Yavuz.

Cross-boundary changes follow Madde 63.

---

# CI Trace Validation

A trace linter SHALL validate at least:

1. registry schema
2. referenced IDs exist
3. retired/superseded ID misuse
4. relation vocabulary
5. duplicate edges
6. machine-detectable dangling refs
7. generated RTM freshness
8. unintended mandatory-coverage regression
9. immutable EvidenceID references
10. stale-evidence use by final claims.

---

# 101. Trace Completeness Is Not Test Success

CI mapping validation SHALL NOT mark a requirement VERIFIED merely because its edges exist.

Actual evidence controls verification.

---

# Coverage Metrics

Generated metrics:

## 102. Allocation Coverage

Requirements with architecture allocation.

## 103. Implementation Coverage

Requirements with implementation refs.

## 104. Verification Design Coverage

Requirements with Test/Benchmark/Drill definitions.

## 105. Evidence Coverage

Requirements with acceptance evidence.

## 106. Final Verification Coverage

Requirements currently VERIFIED.

## 107. Orphan Count

Requirement/test/evidence/claim orphan counts.

---

# 108. Coverage Metrics Are Completeness Metrics, Not Productivity Metrics

---

# 109. 99% Mandatory Coverage Is Not 99% Product PASS

A single blocking requirement may still fail product acceptance.

---

# Milestone Gates

## M2

Foundational spine requirements have:

* architecture allocation
* implementation links
* initial TestIDs.

---

# M3

Every closed-loop F0 has an integrated scenario path.

---

# M4

Required:

> **100% active F0/F1 Implementation Coverage**

---

# M5

Required:

> **100% active F0/F1 Verification Design Coverage**

---

# M6

Required:

> **active F0/F1 ORPHAN-REQ count = 0**

and:

> all H0/A1 NFR measurement definitions complete.

Research-affecting trace semantics freeze.

---

# M7

R1 and FBC evidence traces complete.

---

# M8

Required:

> **100% active F0/F1 final disposition**

> **100% H0/A1 final disposition**

> **active mandatory orphan requirement count = 0**

> **final orphan evidence count = 0**

> **major orphan claim count = 0**

---

# Acceptance Coverage Report

At M8 generate:

> **AcceptanceCoverageReport**

It SHALL answer:

* Which F0/F1 requirements are VERIFIED?
* Which failed?
* Which NFR H0/A1 failed?
* Which S2 missed?
* Which C3 were characterized?
* Which evidence supports each?
* Which release generated that evidence?
* Which evidence is STALE?
* Which requirement lacks evidence?
* Which claims depend on failed/stale evidence?

---

# 110. AcceptanceCoverageReport Is Generated Reproducibly

It is not manually assembled at project end.

---

# Verification Sufficiency by Requirement Class

## F0

Requires:

* implementation
* appropriate local/component verification
* at least one real integrated acceptance path
* final evidence.

---

# F1

Requires:

* implementation
* appropriate verification
* final evidence.

Not every F1 needs E2E.

---

# R1

Requires:

* reproducible research mechanism
* final research evidence.

---

# NFR H0

Requires:

> PASS.

---

# NFR A1

Requires:

> measured threshold PASS.

---

# NFR S2

Requires:

> measured PASS or MISS.

---

# NFR C3

Requires:

> measured characterization.

---

# Test Failure Propagation

A failing linked TestID SHALL identify affected requirements.

However:

> requirement disposition is based on sufficient evidence set.

Not every failed redundant/supporting test automatically makes every linked requirement FAIL.

---

# 111. Failure Disposition Requires Evidence Review

Test defects, redundant test paths and alternate authoritative evidence are distinguished explicitly.

---

# Evidence Authority Levels

Canonical evidence maturity:

## EV-L1 — Development

Local development evidence.

## EV-L2 — CI

Protected automated pipeline evidence.

## EV-L3 — Integration

Shared integrated environment evidence.

## EV-L4 — Formal Evaluation

FBC/formal acceptance execution.

## EV-L5 — Sealed Final

EvidenceSeal-backed final evidence.

---

# 112. Final Quantitative Claims Prefer EV-L5

---

# 113. F0 Final Acceptance Requires Integrated EV-L3+ Evidence

Where formal evaluation applies, EV-L4/EV-L5 is preferred/required.

---

# Verification Boundary Mode

Verification metadata SHOULD identify relevant boundary realism:

> **REAL
> FIXTURE_ALLOWED
> STUB_ALLOWED
> MOCK_ONLY**

---

# 114. F0 Integrated Acceptance Requires REAL Mandatory Boundaries

Mocks/stubs may support lower-level testing but cannot solely verify final integrated F0.

---

# Oracle Taint

Evidence/data nodes SHALL preserve Oracle-taint information.

---

# 115. Oracle-Derived Runtime Input Invalidates Normal Runtime Evidence

`ORACLE_DERIVED` artifacts may verify:

* evaluator correctness
* explicit upper-bound experiment

but cannot prove ordinary operational decision quality where Oracle access is forbidden.

---

# Generated Artifact Traceability

Generated clients/docs SHOULD trace to their source contract where useful.

Requirement mapping prefers:

> source contract identity

over each generated output file.

---

# Migration Traceability

Persisted-domain requirements SHOULD link to relevant schema/migration surfaces when those artifacts materially realize the requirement.

Every historical migration need not remain attached if it no longer changes current semantics.

---

# Model Traceability

ML/Vision requirements SHOULD trace to:

* training/inference implementation
* promoted ModelPackage
* ModelEvaluationRun
* relevant Dataset/Split identities.

---

# RAG Traceability

RAG/RCA requirements SHOULD trace to:

* CorpusVersion
* RetrievalProfile
* retrieval implementation
* formal benchmark.

---

# 116. Evidence Staleness Is Not Code-Only

Corpus/model/config/policy changes may invalidate evidence even when application source does not change.

---

# Workflow Traceability

Automation requirements SHOULD trace to:

* WorkflowBundle
* ActionCatalog
* AuthorityPolicy
* Core command contracts.

---

# Platform Traceability

Platform requirements may trace to:

* Compose
* CI workflows
* deployment workflow
* manifests
* runbooks
* deployment evidence.

Source code is not the only valid realization artifact.

---

# Security Traceability

Security requirements may legitimately cross:

* application policy
* Keycloak configuration
* CI protection
* network/runtime config
* audit system
* security tests.

---

# Runbook Traceability

A runbook may realize a procedural requirement.

Acceptance of that procedure requires its declared drill where one is mandated.

---

# 117. Documentation Does Not Replace Execution Evidence

---

# Research Claim Trace View

Generate a:

> **ResearchClaimTraceView**

containing:

```text
ClaimID
RQ
EvidenceIDs
BenchmarkIDs
RelevantRequirementIDs
ReleaseRef
ClaimStatus
```

---

# 118. Not Every Thesis Sentence Becomes a Claim Node

Use ClaimIDs for:

* major contribution claims
* comparative empirical claims
* product/system acceptance claims
* reproducibility claims.

---

# Human-Readable RTM Views

`03_Requirements_Traceability_Matrix.md` SHALL contain focused views.

## View A — Requirement Master Index

* ID
* class
* owner
* coverage state.

## View B — Architecture Allocation

Requirement → architecture component.

## View C — Implementation Coverage

Requirement → repository/module.

## View D — Verification Coverage

Requirement → TestID/Benchmark/Drill.

## View E — Evidence Coverage

Requirement → final evidence → disposition.

## View F — F0 E2E Coverage

Product-identity requirement → integrated scenario.

## View G — NFR Measurement

Threshold → observed result → status.

## View H — Research Claim Trace

RQ/Claim → evidence.

## View I — Orphan / Stale Evidence

Completeness blockers.

---

# 119. No Unusable Ultra-Wide Master Table

The Markdown document SHALL remain navigable.

Full denormalized export may be provided as:

* CSV
* JSON
* other machine-readable generated artifact.

---

# Ownership Model

## 120. Asrın

Owns:

* requirement semantics
* architecture-level trace coherence.

---

# 121. Yavuz

Owns:

* trace registry tooling
* CI validation
* evidence integration
* report generation.

---

# 122. Capability Owners

Each capability owner maintains semantic correctness of:

* implementation mapping
* verification mapping
* relevant evidence interpretation

for owned requirements.

---

# 123. Yavuz Is Not the Universal RTM Secretary

Tool ownership does not transfer domain mapping responsibility.

---

# Same-PR Trace Rule

Material behavior changes SHOULD update relevant:

* Requirement Impact
* architecture/implementation trace
* contract trace
* TestIDs

within the same PR.

---

# 124. Traceability Is Continuous Engineering Work

It is not deferred to thesis week.

---

# Evidence Linking Timing

Verification definitions may exist before execution.

Actual EvidenceIDs are added only after real evidence exists.

---

# 125. Future EvidenceIDs Shall Not Be Invented

---

# Evidence Immutability

If sealed evidence is superseded:

* old EvidenceID remains immutable
* new evidence receives a new identity
* current applicability is updated.

---

# Superseded Requirement History

Superseded requirements retain:

* source trace
* implementation history
* old verification
* evidence
* historical claims.

They are excluded from current acceptance denominator.

---

# 126. Supersession Cannot Hide Failure

Especially after M6, semantic supersession requires approved change/freeze-impact review.

---

# Completeness vs Correctness

A fully populated RTM may legitimately show:

> system failure.

Traceability exists to expose truth, not manufacture green status.

---

# Traceability Anti-Patterns

Explicitly rejected:

1. manually copying requirement wording into multiple matrices
2. one spreadsheet as sole source of truth
3. mapping every source file manually
4. one test nominally verifying dozens of unrelated requirements
5. GS-01 used as proof of all 306 requirements
6. screenshots used as acceptance evidence by themselves
7. unit test used to prove distributed-failure recovery
8. stale benchmark retained after model/policy change
9. thesis claim linked directly to source code without measured evidence
10. aggregate coverage percentage used to ignore hard failures.

---

# Trace CLI / Query Surface

`mfgctl` or equivalent tooling SHOULD provide:

```text
mfgctl trace validate
mfgctl trace coverage
mfgctl trace requirement FR-AUTO-008
mfgctl trace impacted <artifact>
mfgctl trace orphans
mfgctl trace stale
mfgctl trace acceptance
mfgctl trace generate
```

Exact CLI syntax may evolve.

---

# 127. Requirement Query

A requirement query SHOULD show:

> source → architecture → implementation → tests → current evidence → disposition.

---

# 128. Impact Query

Impact analysis may suggest affected requirements from:

* service
* contract
* model
* workflow
* policy.

It is advisory and does not replace human semantic review.

---

# PR Coverage Summary

Useful PR output:

```text
Impacted requirements:
  FR-SCH-004
  FR-SCH-005

Updated verification:
  TEST-SCH-018
  TEST-SCH-021

Evidence impact:
  Previous SP-NORMAL benchmark becomes STALE
```

---

# ReleaseAcceptanceRecord

Final release acceptance SHALL derive from trace/evidence state.

Introduce:

> **ReleaseAcceptanceRecord**

Suggested fields:

```text
ReleaseManifestRef
RTMBaselineRef
VerifiedF0Count
VerifiedF1Count
VerifiedR1Count
H0Status
A1Status
S2Misses
C3Measured
BlockingFailures
EvidenceSealRef
AcceptanceStatus
```

---

# 129. ReleaseAcceptanceRecord Is Generated

Counts/status SHALL NOT be manually invented.

---

# Final Acceptance Rules

For the candidate final release:

## 130. F0

All active F0:

> VERIFIED.

## 131. F1

All active F1:

> VERIFIED.

## 132. R1

All final mandatory research R1:

> VERIFIED.

## 133. H0

All:

> PASS.

## 134. A1

All:

> PASS.

## 135. S2

All:

> measured with PASS or MISS disposition.

## 136. C3

All:

> measured.

---

# 137. No Active Mandatory `UNKNOWN`

Final acceptance does not permit:

> “untested but probably okay.”

---

# Red-Team Trace Queries

Before M8, the team SHALL be able to answer queries equivalent to:

* show all F0 without integrated evidence
* show all F1 without accepted evidence
* show all H0 without negative/failure verification
* show all A1 measured on wrong HardwareProfile
* show all S2 misses
* show evidence from superseded releases
* show claims relying on stale evidence
* show acceptance-critical tests without requirements
* show requirements affected by a changed event contract
* show mandatory requirements with active high risks/debt.

# RTM Invariants

## RTM-INV-01

RTM is a traceability graph; matrices are generated views.

## RTM-INV-02

Canonical FR/NFR text is not duplicated as independently maintained RTM truth.

## RTM-INV-03

Trace nodes use stable recognized artifact identities.

## RTM-INV-04

Relation vocabulary is controlled.

## RTM-INV-05

Every active F0/F1 traces to approved source decisions.

## RTM-INV-06

Every active F0/F1 has architecture allocation.

## RTM-INV-07

By M4 every active F0/F1 has implementation mapping.

## RTM-INV-08

By M5 every active F0/F1 has verification mapping.

## RTM-INV-09

By M8 every active F0/F1 has sufficient final evidence.

## RTM-INV-10

Every R1 has applicable research evidence.

## RTM-INV-11

Every mandatory NFR traces to an actual measurement mechanism.

## RTM-INV-12

H0/A1 evidence preserves required context.

## RTM-INV-13

Acceptance-critical verification assets trace backward to requirements/invariants.

## RTM-INV-14

Final evidence traces backward to verification intent.

## RTM-INV-15

Major empirical claims trace to evidence.

## RTM-INV-16

Source code cannot substitute for empirical evidence.

## RTM-INV-17

ADR rationale cannot substitute for verification.

## RTM-INV-18

Mock-only verification cannot solely satisfy F0 integration acceptance.

## RTM-INV-19

H0 requires appropriate negative/hard-path evidence.

## RTM-INV-20

S2 MISS is a valid measured disposition.

## RTM-INV-21

C3 requires measurement despite lacking a pass threshold.

## RTM-INV-22

Demo and benchmark evidence remain distinct.

## RTM-INV-23

Evidence applicability considers release/config/model/data/policy context.

## RTM-INV-24

Material behavioral changes may stale evidence.

## RTM-INV-25

Documentation-only change does not automatically stale behavior evidence.

## RTM-INV-26

Model/data/policy changes can stale evidence without source-code change.

## RTM-INV-27

Evidence applicability status is explicit.

## RTM-INV-28

Cross-cutting requirements may map to multiple architecture components while retaining one PrimaryOwner.

## RTM-INV-29

Implementation mapping is not proof.

## RTM-INV-30

Cross-service requirements map to versioned contract identities where applicable.

## RTM-INV-31

Scenarios declare coverage without encoding evaluator answers.

## RTM-INV-32

Every F0 appears in at least one integrated acceptance path.

## RTM-INV-33

GS-01 does not pretend to verify all requirements.

## RTM-INV-34

Quantitative NFR views expose observed values.

## RTM-INV-35

Major empirical claims cannot rely solely on screenshots/source code.

## RTM-INV-36

Literature references do not replace the Manufacturing Operations Platform experimental evidence.

## RTM-INV-37

Major public metric claims trace to sealed evidence/export.

## RTM-INV-38

P0/P1 risks may trace to affected mandatory requirements.

## RTM-INV-39

Technical debt cannot convert H0/A1 failure to PASS.

## RTM-INV-40

Behavior-changing PRs declare Requirement Impact.

## RTM-INV-41

CI validates referenced RequirementIDs.

## RTM-INV-42

Human review remains responsible for semantic impact completeness.

## RTM-INV-43

Breaking contract changes trigger downstream trace/evidence review.

## RTM-INV-44

Trace changes follow capability review ownership.

## RTM-INV-45

Generated RTM remains synchronized with registry.

## RTM-INV-46

Trace completeness cannot fabricate successful verification.

## RTM-INV-47

Coverage metrics measure completeness, not productivity.

## RTM-INV-48

99% coverage cannot compensate for one blocking requirement.

## RTM-INV-49

M6 active mandatory orphan requirement count is zero.

## RTM-INV-50

M8 mandatory requirement/evidence/major-claim orphan count is zero.

## RTM-INV-51

Final AcceptanceCoverageReport is generated reproducibly.

## RTM-INV-52

Verification sufficiency is requirement-class aware.

## RTM-INV-53

F0 final verification includes a real integrated path.

## RTM-INV-54

Failing tests are evaluated against the complete applicable evidence set.

## RTM-INV-55

Final quantitative claims prefer EV-L5 sealed evidence.

## RTM-INV-56

Verification boundary mode is traceable where relevant.

## RTM-INV-57

Oracle-derived evidence cannot verify prohibited runtime behavior.

## RTM-INV-58

Generated artifacts do not become duplicate contract truth.

## RTM-INV-59

Data/model/corpus/workflow identities participate in traceability where behaviorally relevant.

## RTM-INV-60

Security requirements may span application, IdP, CI, network and audit artifacts.

## RTM-INV-61

Operational procedures require drills where acceptance requires executed recovery proof.

## RTM-INV-62

Research Claim Trace covers major claims rather than every thesis sentence.

## RTM-INV-63

RTM is not a marketing database.

## RTM-INV-64

Human-readable RTM uses focused views rather than an unusable ultra-wide matrix.

## RTM-INV-65

Capability owners own semantic correctness of their mappings.

## RTM-INV-66

Yavuz owns tooling/integrity rather than all domain mappings.

## RTM-INV-67

Material trace updates accompany development rather than being deferred.

## RTM-INV-68

Future EvidenceIDs are not fabricated.

## RTM-INV-69

Superseded requirement history remains traceable.

## RTM-INV-70

Requirement supersession cannot conceal post-freeze failure.

## RTM-INV-71

RTM completeness does not imply system correctness.

## RTM-INV-72

Trace tooling supports requirement/orphan/stale/impact/acceptance queries.

## RTM-INV-73

ReleaseAcceptanceRecord is derived from RTM/evidence.

## RTM-INV-74

Final acceptance contains no active mandatory UNKNOWN requirement.

## RTM-INV-75

Traceability exists to expose engineering truth including failures and negative results.

# 84 — E2E Architecture Validation

## Durum

**Approved**

## Amaç

Intelligent Manufacturing Operations Platform for Critical Aerospace Components architecture’sının:

* canonical truth ownership açısından çelişkisiz,
* capability boundaries açısından tutarlı,
* action authority açısından kapalı,
* Sense → Understand → Predict → Decide → Optimize → Execute → Observe → Repeat loop’unu gerçek entegrasyon yollarıyla tamamlayan,
* WorldID / epistemic state / time-domain / Oracle isolation’ı koruyan,
* duplicate / replay / stale / outage / crash / rebuild gibi failure path’lerinde güvenli sonuç üreten,
* bütün F0 capability’leri gerçek E2E yollarına bağlayan,
* ve her takım üyesinin kaldırılmasının farklı bir core product capability’sini kırdığı

bir sistem oluşturduğunu kanıtlayan architecture-level validation modelini tanımlamak.

Canonical lifecycle:

> **Freeze Architecture Baseline → Materialize Authority/Dependency Graphs → Validate Canonical Truth → Validate Closed Loop → Validate Authority Crossings → Validate Isolation → Validate Failure Closure → Validate Recovery Closure → Validate F0 Paths → Execute Architectural Scenarios → Run Role-Removal Analysis → Reconcile RTM → Red-Team Bypasses → Issue Architecture Verdict**

olarak kabul edilmiştir.

Ana prensipler:

> **A Successful Demo Does Not Prove a Valid Architecture**

> **Feedback Cycles Are Expected; Authority Cycles Are Not**

> **Every Protected Action Path Must Close From Proposal to Verified Effect or to an Explicit Safe Failure State**

> **Every Canonical Fact Must Have a Defined Semantic Authority**

> **Every F0 Capability Must Appear on a Real Integrated Path**

> **Removing Any One Team Role Must Break a Distinct Core Product Capability**

---

# Final Architecture Verdict

The final architecture verdict SHALL be one of:

> **ARCHITECTURE_VALID**

or:

> **ARCHITECTURE_INVALID**

No weighted architecture score is used.

During development, individual gates may have:

* PENDING
* BLOCKED
* FAIL
* PASS.

At final M8 validation:

> `PENDING / BLOCKED / UNKNOWN = 0`.

---

Introduce:

> **ArchitectureValidationBaseline**

Conceptual fields:

```text id="4fcgxh"
RequirementBaseline
RTMBaseline
AcceptedADRSet
ContractCatalogVersion
ServiceCatalogVersion

```

Static validation may run before final executable release exists.

Final validation SHALL bind to exact candidate `ReleaseManifest`.

# Architecture Validation Layers

Seven canonical validation layers:

## AVL-1 — Structural

Validates:

* service/component boundaries
* ownership
* dependency structure
* data-authority allocation.

## AVL-2 — Contractual

Validates:

* commands
* events
* APIs
* schemas
* producer/consumer semantics.

## AVL-3 — Authority

Validates who may:

* observe
* infer
* propose
* plan
* validate
* approve
* execute
* mutate.

## AVL-4 — Isolation

Validates:

* WorldID
* epistemic classes
* time domains
* Oracle isolation
* counterfactual separation.

## AVL-5 — Dynamic E2E

Validates successful integrated operational paths.

## AVL-6 — Failure / Recovery

Validates:

* retry
* duplicate
* replay
* crash
* outage
* rebuild
* restart.

## AVL-7 — Product Integrity

Validates:

* F0 closure
* critical paths
* role independence
* reproducibility.

Final architecture validity requires all applicable hard checks across all seven layers to PASS.

# DataAuthorityMap

Architecture validation SHALL maintain:

> **DataAuthorityMap**

Semantic authority is defined by meaning, not merely database location.

Canonical baseline:

| Semantic State                     | Canonical Authority            | Non-Authorities                   |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| Manufacturing business state       | Core                           | Twin, AI, Scheduler, UI           |
| Legal manufacturing transitions    | Core                           | Simulator, Temporal, UI           |
| Physical simulated execution/state | Simulator                      | AI, Scheduler                     |
| Operational projection             | Twin                           | not canonical mutation source     |
| Inspection observation             | Vision                         | AI cannot rewrite observation     |
| RCA hypothesis/inference           | AI                             | not manufacturing fact            |
| Predictive inference               | M1/M2/M3 capability            | not observed fact                 |
| Recovery plan                      | Scheduler                      | not manufacturing effect          |
| Plan feasibility                   | ScheduleValidator              | AI cannot override                |
| Approval decision                  | HITL/Authority subsystem       | AI/Automation cannot self-approve |
| Workflow execution state           | Automation/Temporal            | not manufacturing truth           |
| Human/service identity             | Keycloak                       | frontend not identity authority   |
| Documentary metadata/rights        | PostgreSQL canonical metadata  | Qdrant not rights authority       |
| Retrieval projection               | Qdrant                         | not documentary truth             |
| Immutable artifact bytes           | SeaweedFS                      | metadata/provenance elsewhere     |
| Model promotion identity           | Platform ModelPackage governance | MLflow alone not authority        |
| Telemetry                          | OTel/OpenObserve               | not audit/canonical state         |
| Protected audit                    | audit surface                  | ordinary logs not substitute      |
| Durable transport                  | NATS/JetStream                 | not canonical business database   |
| Cache                              | Valkey where used              | not canonical truth               |

# Canonical Authority Rules

## 1. Exactly One Semantic Authority per Canonical Fact

A canonical semantic fact SHALL NOT have conflicting active authorities.

This does not require:

> one service owns all state.

Different facts may have different authorities.

---

# 2. Twin May Compose Multiple Authoritative Inputs

The Twin may combine canonical inputs into projection state.

It SHALL NOT independently become canonical manufacturing mutation authority.

---

# 3. Derived Stores Remain Derived

The following SHALL NOT silently become canonical operational authorities:

* Twin projection
* Qdrant
* MLflow
* OpenObserve
* Valkey.

---

# WriteAuthorityGraph

Architecture validation SHALL generate:

> **WriteAuthorityGraph**

showing which component may originate/mutate each semantic state.

Forbidden mutation examples:

* AI writing lot state
* Scheduler writing lot state
* Vision placing holds
* browser mutating PostgreSQL
* Twin mutating canonical manufacturing state
* Temporal writing Core tables directly.

---

# Canonical Protected Mutation Path

Protected manufacturing effects SHALL follow the conceptual path:

> **Authorized Intent → Automation → Core Command → Core Validation → Physical/Operational Execution Where Applicable → Canonical Effect Event → Twin Projection → Verification**

The following direct paths are invalid:

> AI → SQL

> UI → Simulator state mutation

> Temporal → Core private database mutation.

---

# Core vs Simulator Boundary

## 4. Core Owns Legal Manufacturing / Business Semantics

The Core governs legal operational transitions.

---

# 5. Simulator Owns Simulated Physical Execution Semantics

The Simulator represents physical operational occurrence in the simulated manufacturing facility.

---

# 6. Simulator SHALL NOT Bypass Core Legal Semantics

Simulator execution cannot create illegal business transitions merely because a physical simulation event occurred.

---

# 7. Core SHALL NOT Become Process-Physics Simulator

Core authority does not imply process-physics ownership.

---

# Feedback Cycles vs Authority Cycles

The normal the Manufacturing Operations Platform control loop is cyclic in time:

> Observe → Decide → Execute → Observe.

This is valid.

A canonical authority cycle is invalid.

Example invalid relationship:

> Core requires Twin to determine canonical state while Twin requires Core to determine that same canonical fact.

---

# 8. Feedback Cycles Are Temporal

They evolve state over time.

---

# 9. Canonical Authority Cycles Are Prohibited

Canonical truth cannot depend on circular authority.

---

# Full Product Loop

The final architecture SHALL collectively realize:

> **Sense → Understand → Predict → Decide → Optimize → Execute → Observe → Repeat**

Canonical allocation:

| Stage      | Primary Capabilities                                    |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sense      | Vision + Simulator operational signals                  |
| Understand | Core / Twin / Genealogy + AI/RCA                        |
| Predict    | M1/M2/M3 + counterfactual simulation where applicable   |
| Decide     | AI structured proposal + deterministic authority policy |
| Optimize   | Scheduler + ScheduleValidator                           |
| Execute    | HITL + Automation + Core/Simulator                      |
| Observe    | Twin + events + Command Center + observability          |
| Repeat     | subsequent event-driven invocation/replanning           |

---

# 10. Capabilities Are Invoked Semantically, Not Artificially

No scenario is required to call every model merely to increase apparent coverage.

The complete acceptance portfolio, however, SHALL integrate every mandatory capability that requires system-level integration.

---

# Forbidden Authority Paths

Architecture validation SHALL explicitly prove absence of:

| Forbidden Path                        | Reason                         |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| AI → Core mutation credential         | AI only READ/SIMULATE/PROPOSE  |
| AI → arbitrary SQL                    | authorization bypass           |
| AI → arbitrary shell                  | security bypass                |
| Scheduler → manufacturing DB mutation | plan ≠ effect                  |
| Vision → lot hold                     | observation ≠ action authority |
| UI → DB protected mutation            | browser untrusted              |
| UI → broker protected command         | browser untrusted              |
| Temporal → private Core DB mutation   | orchestrator must use commands |
| Qdrant content → authorization policy | retrieved text ≠ policy        |
| OpenObserve → manufacturing truth     | telemetry ≠ canonical state    |
| Twin → canonical mutation             | projection ≠ authority         |
| Simulator Oracle → AI/Scheduler       | research integrity violation   |

Any active bypass path is:

> **blocking architecture failure**.

# Approval Architecture

A valid protected approval SHALL bind:

* authenticated human
* exact ActionProposal revision
* exact RecoveryPlan revision where applicable
* WorldID
* relevant entity/state revision/freshness
* applicable risk/authority class.

# 18. Generic Approval Tokens Are Invalid

Approval must bind exact decision content.

# 19. Approval Replay SHALL Fail

# 20. Cross-World Approval SHALL Fail

# 21. Material Plan Mutation Invalidates Prior Approval

> **independent ScheduleValidator**

including:

* Scheduler plan
* AI-suggested plan
* future human-edited plan
* fallback plan.

---

# 22. Generator Cannot Self-Certify Feasibility

A planner cannot mark itself valid without independent validation.

---

# 23. Validator Failure Blocks Execution Eligibility

No AI/human presentation-layer override.

# Automation Outcome Closure

Every protected workflow SHALL terminate in one explicit semantic outcome such as:

> **VERIFIED_SUCCESS**
> **REJECTED**
> **FAILED_KNOWN**
> **UNKNOWN_VERIFY_REQUIRED**
> **CANCELED_BEFORE_EFFECT**

Ambiguous success is prohibited.

---

# 24. Workflow Completion ≠ Manufacturing Completion

---

# 25. Lost ACK Triggers Verification

Blind effect replay is prohibited.

---

# 26. Retry SHALL NOT Duplicate Protected Effect

---

# Protected Command Closure

For every protected command type, architecture SHALL define behavior for:

* request never reaches Core
* Core rejects request
* Core commits but response is lost
* outgoing event publication is delayed
* duplicate request arrives
* duplicate event delivered
* workflow crashes before verification.

Any material undefined branch is an architecture defect.

---

# Event Delivery Architecture

Canonical durable transport assumption:

> **at-least-once delivery**

Architecture validation SHALL cover:

* producer identity
* schema validation
* idempotent consumption
* ordering assumptions
* duplicates
* out-of-order delivery
* poison-message handling
* replay
* gap visibility.

---

# 27. NATS Is Transport, Not Truth

Committed Core truth does not depend solely on broker retention.

---

# 28. Broker Retention Is Not Backup

---

# Outbox Closure

Core mutation + durable outgoing event intent SHALL share the accepted atomic/outbox boundary.

Failure case:

> DB commit succeeds, broker unavailable.

Expected:

> publication intent remains durable.

---

# Consumer Idempotency

Durable state-changing consumers SHALL be tested against duplicate delivery.

Especially:

* Twin
* workflow triggers
* durable projections
* protected automation ingress.

---

Architecture SHALL classify state into at least:

## GLOBAL_IMMUTABLE

* schemas

## WORLD_SCOPED

Examples:

* orders
* lots
* serialized components

* Twin state
* observations
* proposals
* plans
* approvals
* workflows
* commands
* effects.

## EVALUATOR_ONLY

Examples:

* hidden Oracle
* final expected outcomes
* protected challenge labels.

No implicit backend “current world” mutation.
